title.zh: 卷五十七 列傳第十七 蔡廓
title.raw: 卷五十七 列傳第十七 蔡廓 Volume 57 Biographies 17: Cai Kuo

sentences.zh: 列傳第十七 蔡廓子興宗

translations.literal: Biography 17: Cai Kuo; his son Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 17: Cai Kuo and his son Cai Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 蔡廓，字子度，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Kuo, styled Zidu, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Kuo, whose style name was Zidu, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖謨，晉司徒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mo was Jin Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cai Mo had served as Grand Tutor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖系，撫軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Army Aide to the Commander-in-Chief for Expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cai Xi had been secretary to the expeditionary army commander.

sentences.zh: 父綝，司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: His father Shen was Western Attendant on the Left in the Grand Tutor's office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cai Shen had held a secretariat post under the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 廓博涉群書，言行以禮。

translations.literal: Kuo was broadly learned in many books; his words and conduct followed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo had read widely, and in speech and conduct he adhered strictly to propriety.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，時桓玄輔晉，議復肉刑，廓上議曰：「夫建封立法，弘治稽化，必隨時置制，德刑兼施。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant in the Bureau of Writings. At the time Huan Xuan was assisting Jin, there was discussion of restoring corporal punishment. Kuo submitted a memorial, saying: "In establishing feudal orders and enacting laws, in broadly governing and assimilating transformation, one must set institutions according to the times, applying both virtue and punishment together."
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as an assistant in the imperial archives. While Huan Xuan dominated the Jin court, a proposal was put forward to restore mutilation penalties. Kuo submitted a memorial that began: "To establish feudal order and legislate, to govern broadly and foster transformation, institutions must be tailored to their era, with moral suasion and penal sanctions employed together."

sentences.zh: 貞一以閑其邪，教禁以檢其慢，灑湛露以膏潤，厲嚴霜以肅威，晞風者陶和而安恬，畏戾者聞憲而警慮。

translations.literal: Integrity and unity restrain wickedness; teaching and prohibition check presumption. Sprinkling heavy dew moistens and nourishes; deploying stern frost awes and disciplines. Those who feel the breeze are molded to harmony and dwell in peace; those who fear law hear the statutes and are stirred to caution.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity restrains wicked impulses; instruction and prohibition curb arrogance. Like heavy dew, clemency nourishes the people; like bitter frost, severity awes them. Those who feel the gentle breeze are shaped toward harmony and live at ease; those who fear the law hear the statutes and are moved to caution.

sentences.zh: 雖復質文迭用，而斯道莫革。

translations.literal: Although substance and ornament alternated in use, this principle was never altered.
translations.idiomatic: Though the outward forms of governance changed from age to age, this underlying principle never changed.

sentences.zh: 肉刑之設，肇自哲王。

translations.literal: The institution of corporal punishment originated with the sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was first instituted by the sage kings of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 蓋由曩世風淳，民多惇謹，圖像既陳，則機心冥戢，刑人在塗，則不逞改操，故能勝殘去殺，化隆無為。

translations.literal: This was because in former ages customs were pure and the people mostly honest and cautious. Once images were displayed, scheming minds were silently stilled; when punished men were on the roads, they did not dare change their conduct. Thus they could overcome cruelty and remove killing, and transformation flourished in non-action.
translations.idiomatic: In those earlier ages customs were pure and the people for the most part honest and cautious. Once the penal images were displayed, scheming minds fell silent; when branded convicts walked the roads, men did not dare change their ways. That was how the state could overcome cruelty, abolish killing, and bring about a flourishing age of effortless governance.

sentences.zh: 季末澆偽，法網彌密，利巧之懷日滋，恥畏之情轉寡，終身劇役，不足止其奸，況乎黥劓，豈能反其善！

translations.literal: At the end of an age customs became shallow and false; the legal net grew ever tighter. Hearts bent on profit and craft multiplied daily; feelings of shame and fear grew ever thinner. Lifelong hard labor was not enough to stop their wickedness—how much less could tattooing and cutting the nose turn them back to goodness!
translations.idiomatic: By the late age customs had turned shallow and false, and the legal net grew ever tighter. Hearts bent on profit and cunning multiplied day by day, while shame and fear dwindled. Lifelong hard labor could not stop their wickedness—how could branding and mutilation restore them to goodness?

sentences.zh: 徒有酸慘之聲，而無濟治之益。

translations.literal: There were only sounds of bitter suffering, with no benefit to aiding good order.
translations.idiomatic: They produced only cries of bitter suffering, with no benefit to good governance.

sentences.zh: 至於棄市之條，實非不赦之罪，事非手殺，考律同歸，輕重均科，減降路塞，鍾、陳以之抗言，元皇所為留愍。

translations.literal: As for the statute on execution at the marketplace, it was in truth not a crime beyond pardon; when the deed was not killing by one's own hand, examination of the law treated it the same. Light and heavy were punished alike, and the path of reduction and commutation was blocked. Zhong and Chen spoke against this on principle, and Emperor Yuan retained his compassion on that account.
translations.idiomatic: As for the statute prescribing execution at the marketplace, the offense was not one beyond all pardon; when a man had not killed with his own hand, the law still treated the case the same. Light and heavy offenses received the same sentence, and the path to reduction or commutation was blocked. Zhong Yao and Chen Qun protested on principle, and Emperor Yuan of Jin showed compassion for that reason.

sentences.zh: 今英輔翼贊，道邈伊、周，雖閉否之運甫開，而遐遺之難未已。

translations.literal: Now worthy assistants flank and support the throne; the Way rivals that of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Although the cycle of obstruction and denial has just begun to open, the hardships of distant legacy have not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Now worthy ministers flank the throne, and the governance aspires to the stature of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Though the age of obstruction is just beginning to lift, the hardships left by a distant legacy have not yet ended.

sentences.zh: 誠宜明慎用刑，愛民弘育，申哀矜以革濫，移大辟於支體，全性命之至重，恢繁息於將來。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to be clear and cautious in the use of punishments, to cherish the people and broadly nurture them, to extend compassion and pity to reform excess, to shift capital punishment to the limbs, to preserve the utmost weight of life, and to restore flourishing increase for the future.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly fitting to use punishments with clarity and caution, to cherish the people and nurture them broadly, to extend compassion and pity in order to curb excess, to replace capital punishment with mutilation of the limbs, to preserve what is most precious in human life, and to restore growth and repose for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 使將斷之骨，荷更榮於三陽，干時之華，監商飆而知懼。

translations.literal: Let bones about to be severed bear renewed glory in the three yang months; let the flowers of the age, beholding the autumn gale, know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Let those whose limbs were about to be severed instead regain their wholeness in the spring; let the proud men of the age, seeing the autumn wind, learn fear.

sentences.zh: 威惠俱宣，感畏偕設，全生拯暴，於是乎在。」

translations.literal: When awe and kindness are both proclaimed, when feeling and fear are jointly established, preserving life and rescuing from violence—therein it lies."
translations.idiomatic: When awe and kindness are both made manifest, when gratitude and fear are instilled together, the preservation of life and deliverance from violence will be achieved—this is the way."

sentences.zh: 遷司徒主簿，尚書度支殿中郎，通直郎，高祖太尉參軍，司徒屬，中書、黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Registrar in the Grand Tutor's office, Palace Attendant in the Revenue Section of the Secretariat, Direct Communication Gentleman, staff officer to the Grand Marshal under the Founding Emperor, staff member of the Grand Tutor, and Gentleman of the Central Secretariat and Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of registrar in the Grand Tutor's office, palace attendant in the revenue section of the Secretariat, direct communication gentleman, staff officer to the Grand Marshal under Emperor Wu of Song, secretariat aide to the Grand Tutor, and gentleman of the Central Secretariat and Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 以方鯁閑素，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Because of his upright firmness and plain simplicity, he was noticed by the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His upright character and plain, unadorned manner won the notice of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 及高祖領兗州，廓為別駕從事史，委以州任。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took charge of Yan Province, Kuo served as Registrar Aide and was entrusted with the affairs of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took charge of Yan Province, Kuo served as registrar aide and was entrusted with the full administration of the province.

sentences.zh: 尋除中軍諮議參軍，太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Consulting Staff Officer in the Central Army and Attendant in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed consulting staff officer in the central army and attendant in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遭母憂。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, he suffered the loss of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post, his mother died.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，三年不櫛沐，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: By nature he was utterly filial; for three years he did not comb his hair or bathe, and he nearly could not survive his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial; for the full three-year mourning period he neither combed his hair nor bathed, and he nearly succumbed to grief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，相國府復板為從事中郎，領記室。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the Chancellor's office again appointed him Attendant and put him in charge of the Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, the chancellor's office reappointed him attendant and placed him in charge of the records office.

sentences.zh: 宋臺建，為侍中，建議以為：「鞫獄不宜令子孫下辭明言父祖之罪，虧教傷情，莫此為大。

translations.literal: When the Song regime was established, he became Palace Attendant and submitted a proposal, saying: "In interrogating cases, one should not require descendants to submit written statements explicitly stating the crimes of their fathers and grandfathers. Nothing does greater harm to teaching and to human feeling than this."
translations.idiomatic: When the Song regime was established, he became palace attendant and proposed: "In criminal interrogations, descendants should not be required to submit written statements explicitly naming the crimes of their fathers and grandfathers. Nothing does greater harm to moral instruction and human feeling."

sentences.zh: 自今但令家人與囚相見，無乞鞫之訴，使足以明伏罪，不須責家人下辭。

translations.literal: From now on let only family members meet the prisoner, without petitions for re-interrogation, so that guilt may be made clear enough; there is no need to require family members to submit statements.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let family members meet the prisoner without petitions for re-interrogation, so that guilt may be established clearly enough, without requiring relatives to submit written statements.

sentences.zh: 」朝議咸以為允，從之。

translations.literal: " The court discussion unanimously approved, and the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court unanimously approved, and the measure was adopted.

sentences.zh: 世子左衛率謝靈運輒殺人，御史中丞王准之坐不糾免官，高祖以廓剛直，不容邪枉，補御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun, Left Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent, killed a man on his own authority. Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhunzhi was dismissed for failing to impeach. The Founding Emperor, because Kuo was upright and firm and would not tolerate crookedness, appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun, commander of the heir apparent's left guard, killed a man on his own authority. Censor-in-chief Wang Zhunzhi was dismissed for failing to impeach him. Emperor Wu, knowing Kuo's upright and unyielding character and his intolerance of wrongdoing, appointed Kuo censor-in-chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 多所糾奏，百僚震肅。

translations.literal: He impeached many cases, and the hundred officials were awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached many officials, and the entire bureaucracy was awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 時中書令傅亮任寄隆重，學冠當時，朝廷儀典，皆取定於亮，每咨廓然後施行。

translations.literal: At the time Central Secretariat Director Fu Liang held weighty trust and his learning topped the age. Court ritual and statutes were all decided by Liang, who consulted Kuo before putting them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fu Liang, director of the Central Secretariat, held great authority and his learning surpassed that of his contemporaries. Court ritual and protocol were all settled by Liang, who consulted Kuo before implementing them.

sentences.zh: 亮意若有不同，廓終不為屈。

translations.literal: If Liang's view differed, Kuo would never yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's view differed, Kuo never yielded.

sentences.zh: 時疑揚州刺史廬陵王義真朝堂班次，亮與廓書曰：「揚州自應著刺史服耳。

translations.literal: At the time there was doubt about the court seating order of the Prince of Luling, Yizhen, as Governor of Yang Province. Liang wrote to Kuo, saying: "Yang Province should of course wear the governor's robes."
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was uncertainty about the court seating order of Prince Yizhen of Luling, governor of Yang Province. Liang wrote to Kuo: "As governor of Yang Province, he should of course wear the robes of a provincial governor."

sentences.zh: 然謂坐起班次，應在朝堂諸官上，不應依官次坐下。

translations.literal: Yet I hold that in seating order for sitting and rising, he should rank above the officials of the court hall and should not be seated according to official rank.
translations.idiomatic: But in seating order for court sessions, he should rank above the other officials in the hall and should not take his seat according to ordinary official precedence.

sentences.zh: 足下試更尋之。

translations.literal: Please search the precedents again.
translations.idiomatic: Please look into the precedents again.

sentences.zh: 《詩序》云『王姬下嫁於諸侯，衣服禮秩，不係其夫，下王后一等。

translations.literal: The Preface to the Odes says: "When a king's daughter marries down to a feudal lord, her dress and ritual rank are not tied to her husband's; she ranks one grade below the queen."
translations.idiomatic: The Preface to the Book of Odes states: "When a king's daughter marries down to a feudal lord, her dress and ritual rank are not bound to her husband's; she ranks one grade below the queen."

sentences.zh: 』推王姬下王后一等，則皇子居然在王公之上。

translations.literal: " Inferring that a king's daughter ranks one grade below the queen, then an imperial prince plainly ranks above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: " By that analogy, an imperial prince plainly ranks above kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 陸士衡《起居注》，式乾殿集，諸皇子悉在三司上。

translations.literal: Lu Shiheng's Court Diary records that at the assembly in Shiqian Hall, all imperial princes were above the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's Court Diary records that at the assembly in Shiqian Hall, all imperial princes were seated above the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 今抄疏如別。

translations.literal: I now copy the relevant passage separately.
translations.idiomatic: I enclose a copy of the relevant passage separately.

sentences.zh: 又海西即位赦文，太宰武陵王第一，撫軍將軍會稽王第二，大司馬第三。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the amnesty proclamation when Haixi ascended the throne, Grand Preceptor Prince Wuling was first, General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Kuaiji second, and Grand Marshal third.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the amnesty proclamation when Emperor Haixi ascended the throne, Grand Preceptor Prince Wuling was listed first, General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Kuaiji second, and Grand Marshal third.

sentences.zh: 大司馬位既最高，又都督中外，而次在二王之下，豈非下皇子邪？

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal's position was already the highest, and he also commanded internal and external forces—yet he ranked below the two princes. Is this not placing him below imperial princes?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal held the highest position and also commanded all military forces—yet he was listed below the two princes. Does this not show that he ranked below imperial princes?

sentences.zh: 此文今具在也。

translations.literal: This document still exists in full today.
translations.idiomatic: That document still survives in full.

sentences.zh: 永和中，蔡公為司徒，司馬簡文為撫軍開府，對錄朝政。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era, Duke Cai was Grand Tutor and Sima Jianwen opened an office as General Who Pacifies the Army; they jointly recorded court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghe era, Duke Cai served as Grand Tutor while Sima Jianwen opened an office as General Who Pacifies the Army; they jointly oversaw court affairs.

sentences.zh: 蔡為正司，不應反在儀同之下，而于時位次，相王在前，蔡公次之耳。

translations.literal: Cai held the regular chief office and should not have ranked below an equal in ceremonial honor—yet at that time in seating order the Prince of Xiang was ahead and Duke Cai second.
translations.idiomatic: Cai held the regular chief office and should not have ranked below a ceremonial equal—yet at that time the Prince of Xiang was seated ahead and Duke Cai second.

sentences.zh: 諸例甚多，不能復具疏。

translations.literal: There are many such precedents; I cannot list them all in detail.
translations.idiomatic: There are many such precedents, which I cannot list in full here.

sentences.zh: 揚州反乃居卿君之下，恐此失禮，宜改之邪？

translations.literal: Yet Yang Province ranks below you and the lord—this may be a breach of ritual. Should it be changed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the governor of Yang Province ranks below you and the lord—this may be a breach of ritual. Should it be changed?

sentences.zh: 」廓答曰：「揚州位居卿君之下，常亦惟疑。

translations.literal: " Kuo replied: "That Yang Province ranks below you and the lord has always been a matter of doubt for me as well."
translations.idiomatic: " Kuo replied: "That the governor of Yang Province ranks below you and the lord has always troubled me as well."

sentences.zh: 然朝廷以位相次，不以本封，復無明文云皇子加殊禮。

translations.literal: Yet the court orders rank by office in succession, not by original enfeoffment, and there is again no explicit text saying that imperial princes receive special ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court orders precedence by actual office, not by original enfeoffment, and there is no explicit statute granting imperial princes special ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 齊獻王為驃騎，孫秀來降，武帝欲優異之，以秀為驃騎，轉齊王為鎮軍，在驃騎上。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi was Rapid Cavalry General. When Sun Xiu came over in surrender, Emperor Wu wished to honor him specially: he made Xiu Rapid Cavalry General and transferred the Prince of Qi to Pacifying Army General, ranking above Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi was Rapid Cavalry General. When Sun Xiu surrendered, Emperor Wu wished to honor him specially: he made Xiu Rapid Cavalry General and transferred the Prince of Qi to Pacifying Army General, ranking above the Rapid Cavalry post.

sentences.zh: 若如足下言，皇子便在公右，則齊王本次自尊，何改鎮軍，令在驃騎上，明知故依見位為次也。

translations.literal: If, as you say, an imperial prince is by nature to the right of dukes, then the Prince of Qi's rank was already honorable in itself—why change him to Pacifying Army General and place him above Rapid Cavalry? Clearly they knowingly followed present office for order.
translations.idiomatic: If, as you say, an imperial prince by nature ranks above dukes, then the Prince of Qi's standing was already honorable—why transfer him to Pacifying Army General and place him above Rapid Cavalry? Clearly the court knowingly followed actual office for precedence.

sentences.zh: 又齊王為司空，賈充為太尉，俱錄尚書署事，常在充後。

translations.literal: Again, when the Prince of Qi was Minister of Works and Jia Chong was Grand Marshal, both recording Secretariat affairs, the prince was regularly behind Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when the Prince of Qi was Minister of Works and Jia Chong was Grand Marshal, both recording Secretariat affairs, the prince consistently ranked behind Chong.

sentences.zh: 潘正叔奏《公羊》事，于時三錄，梁王肜為衛將軍，署在太尉隴西王泰、司徒王玄沖下。

translations.literal: When Pan Zhengshu presented a matter on the Gongyang Commentary, at that time the three recorders included Prince Rong of Liang as Defender General, whose signature was below Grand Marshal Prince Tai of Longxi and Grand Tutor Wang Xuanchong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Zhengshu presented a matter on the Gongyang Commentary, among the three recorders Prince Rong of Liang, as Defender General, signed below Grand Marshal Prince Tai of Longxi and Grand Tutor Wang Xuanchong.

sentences.zh: 近太元初，賀新宮成，司馬太傅為中軍，而以齊王柔之為賀首。

translations.literal: Recently, at the beginning of the Taiyuan era, when the new palace was completed for celebration, Sima the Grand Preceptor was Central Army Commander, yet Prince Rouzhi of Qi was made head of the celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, at the beginning of the Taiyuan era, when celebrations for the new palace were held, Sima the Grand Preceptor was central army commander, yet Prince Rouzhi of Qi was made head of the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 立安帝為太子，上禮，徐邈為郎，位元次亦以太傅在諸王下；

translations.literal: When Emperor An was established as heir apparent and the ascending rites were performed, Xu Miao was a gentleman, and in seating order the Grand Preceptor too was below the princes;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An was installed as heir apparent and the ascending rites were performed, Xu Miao was a gentleman, and in seating order the Grand Preceptor too was placed below the princes;

sentences.zh: 又謁李太后，宗正尚書符令以高密王為首，時王東亭為僕射。

translations.literal: again, when paying homage to Empress Dowager Li, the Minister of the Imperial Clan and Secretariat order placed Prince of Gaomi first, at a time when Wang Dongting was Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: again, when paying homage to Empress Dowager Li, the order from the Minister of the Imperial Clan and the Secretariat placed the Prince of Gaomi first, at a time when Wang Dongting was vice director.

sentences.zh: 王、徐皆是近世識古今者。

translations.literal: Wang and Xu were both men of recent times who knew past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Xu were both recent authorities who knew past and present precedent.

sentences.zh: 足下引式乾公王，吾謂未可為據。

translations.literal: You cite the princes at Shiqian— I say that cannot serve as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: You cite the assembly at Shiqian Hall—I do not think that can serve as evidence.

sentences.zh: 其云上出式乾，召侍中彭城王植、荀組、潘嶽、嵇紹、杜斌，然後道足下所疏四王，在三司之上，反在黃門郎下，有何義？

translations.literal: It says the emperor went out to Shiqian and summoned Palace Attendant Prince Zhi of Pengcheng, Xun Zu, Pan Yue, Ji Shao, and Du Bin—then mentions the four princes you cited, above the Three Excellencies yet below Yellow Gate Gentlemen. What sense is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: It says the emperor went out to Shiqian and summoned palace attendant Prince Zhi of Pengcheng, Xun Zu, Pan Yue, Ji Shao, and Du Bin—then lists the four princes you cited, above the Three Excellencies yet below yellow gate gentlemen. What sense does that make?

sentences.zh: 且四王之下則云大將軍梁王肜、車騎趙王倫，然後云司徒王戎耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, below the four princes it names Great General Prince Rong of Liang and Chariots-and-Cavalry Prince Lun of Zhao, and only then Grand Tutor Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Below the four princes, the roster lists Great General Prince Rong of Liang and Chariots-and-Cavalry Prince Lun of Zhao first—only then does it mention Grand Tutor Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 梁、趙二王亦是皇子，屬尊位齊，在豫章王常侍之下，又復不通。

translations.literal: The princes of Liang and Zhao were also imperial princes, of comparable honored rank, yet placed below Prince Changshi of Yuzhang—again inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Liang and Zhao were also imperial princes of comparable rank, yet placed below Prince Changshi of Yuzhang—again inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 蓋書家指疏時事，不必存其班次；

translations.literal: Writers merely record current affairs in summary and need not preserve seating order;
translations.idiomatic: Historians merely record current affairs in summary and need not preserve seating order;

sentences.zh: 式乾亦是私宴，異於朝堂。

translations.literal: Shiqian was also a private banquet, different from the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was also a private banquet, different from a formal court session.

sentences.zh: 如今含章西堂，足下在僕射下，侍中在尚書下耳。

translations.literal: As now in the western hall of Hanzhang, you rank below the Vice Director, and the Palace Attendant below the Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As in the western hall of Hanzhang today, you rank below the vice director, and the palace attendant below the director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 來示又云曾祖與簡文對錄，位在簡文下。

translations.literal: Your letter also says my great-grandfather jointly recorded affairs with Jianwen and ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter also states that my great-grandfather jointly recorded affairs with Emperor Jianwen and ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 吾家故事則不然，今寫如別。

translations.literal: Our family's established practice was not so; I now write it out separately.
translations.idiomatic: Our family's established practice was otherwise; I enclose the record separately.

sentences.zh: 王姬身無爵位，故可得不從夫而以王女為尊。

translations.literal: A king's daughter personally holds no noble rank, so she may not follow her husband and instead honor the king's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: A king's daughter holds no noble rank in her own person, so she need not follow her husband's rank and may be honored as the king's daughter.

sentences.zh: 皇子出任則有位，有位則依朝，復示之班序。

translations.literal: When an imperial prince takes office he has a position; having a position, he follows the court and again displays court seating order.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial prince takes office he holds a post; holding a post, he follows court precedence and is seated accordingly.

sentences.zh: 唯引泰和赦文，差可為言。

translations.literal: Only your citation of the Taihe amnesty can somewhat serve as argument.
translations.idiomatic: Only your citation of the Taihe amnesty can somewhat support your case.

sentences.zh: 然赦文前後，亦參差不同。

translations.literal: Yet amnesty texts before and after also differ unevenly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet amnesty proclamations before and after that also vary inconsistently.

sentences.zh: 太宰上公，自應在大司馬前耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, as senior lord, should naturally be before the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, as senior lord, should naturally precede the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 簡文雖撫軍，時已授丞相殊禮，又中外都督，故以本任為班，不以督中外便在公右也。

translations.literal: Although Jianwen was General Who Pacifies the Army, at the time he had already been granted the Chancellor's special honors and also commanded internal and external forces—thus his original office set his order, not that commanding internal and external forces placed him to the right of dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jianwen was General Who Pacifies the Army, he had already been granted the chancellor's special honors and also commanded all military forces—thus his original office determined his precedence, not the fact that he commanded all forces.

sentences.zh: 今護軍揔方伯，而位次故在持節都督下，足下復思之。」

translations.literal: Today the Protector of the Army commands the regional lords, yet his rank is still below the Commissioner with the Staff—please reconsider."
translations.idiomatic: Today the Protector of the Army commands the regional governors, yet his rank still falls below a commissioner with the staff of authority—please reconsider."

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左長史，出為豫章太守，徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Clerk on the Left in the Grand Tutor's office, went out as Governor of Yuzhang, and was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief clerk on the left in the Grand Tutor's office, served as governor of Yuzhang, and was summoned to be director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廓因北地傅隆問亮：「選事若悉以見付，不論；

translations.literal: Kuo had Fu Long of Beidi ask Liang: "If the selection affairs are entirely entrusted to me, I have no objection;
translations.idiomatic: Kuo sent Fu Long of Beidi to ask Liang: "If you entrust the whole of selection affairs to me, I have no objection;

sentences.zh: 不然，不能拜也。

translations.literal: otherwise I cannot accept the appointment."
translations.idiomatic: but otherwise I cannot take the post."

sentences.zh: 」亮以語錄尚書徐羨之，羨之曰：「黃門郎以下，悉以委蔡，吾徒不復厝懷；

translations.literal: " Liang told Recorder of the Secretariat Xu Xianzhi, who said: "From Yellow Gate Gentleman downward, entrust all to Cai; we need no longer concern ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: " Liang told Recorder of the Secretariat Xu Xianzhi, who said: "From yellow gate gentleman downward, entrust everything to Cai; we need no longer concern ourselves;

sentences.zh: 自此以上，故宜共參同異。

translations.literal: from that rank upward, we should jointly deliberate differences."
translations.idiomatic: from that rank upward, we should jointly deliberate."

sentences.zh: 」廓曰：「我不能為徐干木署紙尾也。

translations.literal: " Kuo said: "I cannot sign at the bottom of the yellow paper for Xu Ganmu."
translations.idiomatic: " Kuo said: "I will not countersign the yellow paper at the bottom for Xu Ganmu."

sentences.zh: 」遂不拜。

translations.literal: " He therefore did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 干木，羨之小字也。

translations.literal: Ganmu was Xianzhi's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Ganmu" was the childhood name of Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 選案黃紙，錄尚書與吏部尚書連名，故廓云：「署紙尾」也。

translations.literal: Selection cases used yellow paper on which the Recorder of the Secretariat and the Director of Personnel signed jointly—hence Kuo's words about "signing at the paper's end."
translations.idiomatic: Selection cases used yellow paper on which the Recorder of the Secretariat and the Director of Personnel signed jointly—hence Kuo's remark about "signing at the paper's end."

sentences.zh: 羨之亦以廓正直，不欲使居權要。

translations.literal: Xianzhi also, because Kuo was upright, did not wish him to hold a position of power.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi also, knowing Kuo's upright character, did not wish him to hold a position of power.

sentences.zh: 徙為祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太祖入奉大統，尚書令傅亮率百僚奉迎，廓亦俱行。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor entered to receive the great succession, Secretariat Director Fu Liang led the hundred officials to welcome him, and Kuo went along as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen entered to receive the imperial succession, Secretariat Director Fu Liang led the officials to welcome him, and Kuo went along as well.

sentences.zh: 至尋陽，遇疾，不堪前。

translations.literal: At Xunyang he fell ill and could not go on.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang he fell ill and could not continue.

sentences.zh: 亮將進路，詣廓別，廓謂曰：「營陽在吳，宜厚加供奉。

translations.literal: Liang was about to advance and came to bid Kuo farewell. Kuo said to him: "The Lord of Yingyang is in Wu; he should be generously supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was about to continue and came to bid Kuo farewell. Kuo said to him: "The Lord of Yingyang is in Wu; he should be generously provided for.

sentences.zh: 營陽不幸，卿諸人有弑主之名，欲立於世，將可得邪！

translations.literal: If misfortune befalls the Lord of Yingyang, you gentlemen will bear the name of regicide. Wishing to stand in the world—how can that be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune befalls the Lord of Yingyang, you will bear the name of regicides. Do you think you can still stand honorably in the world?

sentences.zh: 」亮已與羨之議害少帝，乃馳信止之，信至，已不及。

translations.literal: " Liang had already discussed harming the young emperor with Xianzhi and therefore sent a fast message to stop it, but when the message arrived it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang had already plotted with Xianzhi to harm the young emperor and therefore sent an urgent message to stop it, but when the message arrived it was too late.

sentences.zh: 羨之大怒曰：「與人共計議，云何裁轉背，便賣惡於人。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greatly angered and said: "When one plots together with others, how can one suddenly turn about and shift the blame onto others?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was furious and said: "When men plot together, how can one suddenly turn about and shift the blame onto others?"

sentences.zh: 」及太祖即位，謝晦將之荊州，與廓別，屏人問曰：「吾其免乎？

translations.literal: " When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xie Hui was about to go to Jing Province. Bidding Kuo farewell, he dismissed attendants and asked: "Will I escape harm?"
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xie Hui was departing for Jing Province. Bidding Kuo farewell, he dismissed his attendants and asked: "Will I escape harm?"

sentences.zh: 」廓曰：「卿受先帝顧命，任以社稷，廢昏立明，義無不可。

translations.literal: " Kuo said: "You received the late emperor's dying charge and were entrusted with the altars of state. Deposing the dim and establishing the bright—nothing in principle forbids it.
translations.idiomatic: " Kuo said: "You received the late emperor's dying charge and were entrusted with the state. Deposing a dim ruler and establishing a bright one—nothing in principle forbids that.

sentences.zh: 但殺人二昆，而以之北面，挾震主之威，據上流之重，以古推今，自免為難也。」

translations.literal: But you killed two imperial brothers and yet have them face north in homage; you wield the awe of one who terrifies his lord and hold the weight of the upper reaches. Judging the present by antiquity, escaping harm for yourself will be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: But you killed two imperial brothers and yet have them pay homage facing north; you wield the awe of one who terrifies his lord and hold command of the upper Yangzi. Judging the present by antiquity, you will find it hard to escape harm."

sentences.zh: 廓年位並輕，而為時流所推重，每至歲時，皆束帶到門。

translations.literal: Kuo's age and rank were both light, yet the leading men of the age esteemed him; at each year's turn they all came to his door in formal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Though Kuo was young and held modest rank, the leading men of the age esteemed him; at each year's turn they all came to his door in formal dress.

sentences.zh: 奉兄軌如父，家事小大，皆咨而後行；

translations.literal: He served his elder brother Gui as a father; in household matters great and small he consulted before acting;
translations.idiomatic: He served his elder brother Gui as he would a father; in household matters great and small he consulted Gui before acting;

sentences.zh: 公祿賞賜，一皆入軌，有所資須，悉就典者請焉。

translations.literal: official salary and rewards all went to Gui; whatever he needed he entirely requested from the steward.
translations.idiomatic: official salary and rewards all went to Gui; whatever he needed he requested from the household steward.

sentences.zh: 從高祖在彭城，妻郗氏書求夏服，廓答書曰：「知須夏服，計給事自應相供，無容別寄。

translations.literal: When he followed the Founding Emperor at Pengcheng, his wife Lady Xi wrote asking for summer garments. Kuo replied: "I know summer garments are needed; the household steward should supply them—there is no occasion to send them separately.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Wu at Pengcheng, his wife Lady Xi wrote asking for summer garments. Kuo replied: "I know you need summer garments; the household steward should supply them—there is no need to send them separately.

sentences.zh: 」時軌為給事中。

translations.literal: " At the time Gui was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Gui was palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，廓卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Kuo died at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia (425), Kuo died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗云：「羊徽、蔡廓，可平世三公。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor once said: "Yang Hui and Cai Kuo could be the Three Excellencies of a peaceful age.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once said: "Yang Hui and Cai Kuo could serve as the Three Excellencies in a peaceful age.

sentences.zh: 」少子興宗。

translations.literal: " His youngest son was Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: " His youngest son was named Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 興宗年十歲失父，哀毀有異凡童。

translations.literal: Xingzong lost his father at the age of ten; his grief and devastation differed from ordinary children.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong lost his father at the age of ten, and his grief and devastation were unlike those of ordinary children.

sentences.zh: 廓罷豫章郡還，起二宅。

translations.literal: When Kuo left the governorship of Yuzhang and returned, he built two residences.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuo left the governorship of Yuzhang and returned home, he built two residences.

sentences.zh: 先成東宅，與軌；

translations.literal: He first completed the eastern residence and gave it to Gui;
translations.idiomatic: He first completed the eastern residence and gave it to his brother Gui;

sentences.zh: 廓亡而館宇未立，軌罷長沙郡還，送錢五十萬以補宅直。

translations.literal: Kuo died before the halls were finished. Gui, returning from leaving the commandery of Changsha, sent five hundred thousand in cash to cover the cost of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo died before the buildings were finished. Gui, returning after leaving the governorship of Changsha, sent five hundred thousand cash to cover the cost of the house.

sentences.zh: 興宗年十歲，白母曰：「一家由來豐儉必共，今日宅價不宜受也。

translations.literal: Xingzong, aged ten, told his mother: "Our family has always shared abundance and want alike; today we should not accept the price of the house."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong, aged ten, told his mother: "Our family has always shared abundance and want alike; we should not accept the price of the house today."

sentences.zh: 」母悅而從焉。

translations.literal: " His mother was pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother was delighted and assented.

sentences.zh: 軌有愧色，謂其子淡曰：「我年六十，行事不及十歲小兒。

translations.literal: Gui showed a look of shame and said to his son Dan: "I am sixty years old, yet in conduct I fall short of a ten-year-old child."
translations.idiomatic: Gui looked ashamed and said to his son Dan: "I am sixty years old, yet in conduct I fall short of a ten-year-old child."

sentences.zh: 」尋喪母。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward his mother died.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以業尚素立見稱。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was praised for establishing himself through plain, upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and won praise for establishing himself through plain, upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 初為彭城王義康司徒行參軍，太子舍人，南平穆王冠軍參軍，武昌太守。

translations.literal: He first served as Secretariat Aide to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent, staff officer to the Champion General under the Prince of Nanping, and Governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as secretariat aide to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, staff officer to the champion general under the Prince of Nanping, and governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 又為太子洗馬，義陽王友，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He also served as Groom of the Heir Apparent, Companion to the Prince of Yiyang, and Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as groom of the heir apparent, companion to the Prince of Yiyang, and secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 中書令建平王宏、侍中王僧綽並與興宗厚善。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Prince Hong of Jianping and Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo were both on close terms with Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Central Secretariat Director Prince Hong of Jianping and palace attendant Wang Sengchuo were both on close terms with Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，僧綽被誅，凶威方盛，親故莫敢往，興宗獨臨哭盡哀。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne by regicide, Sengchuo was executed. The tyrant's power was at its height and kin and friends dared not go near; Xingzong alone came to mourn and wept his full grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper seized the throne by regicide, Sengchuo was executed. The tyrant's power was at its height and kin and friends dared not approach; Xingzong alone came to mourn and wept his full grief.

sentences.zh: 出為司空何尚之長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to Minister of Works He Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief clerk to Minister of Works He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 又遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Senior Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to senior attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，還先職，遷臨海太守，徵為黃門郎，太子中庶子，轉游擊將軍，俄遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Xingzong returned to his former post, was moved to Governor of Linhai, summoned as Yellow Gate Gentleman and Senior Attendant of the Heir Apparent, transferred to General of Roaming Attack, and soon promoted to Secretariat Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Xingzong returned to his former post, became governor of Linhai, was summoned as yellow gate gentleman and senior attendant of the heir apparent, transferred to general of roaming attack, and soon promoted to secretariat gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時尚書何偃疾患，上謂興宗曰：「卿詳練清濁，今以選事相付，便可開門當之，無所讓也。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Director He Yan was ill. The emperor said to Xingzong: "You are well versed in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy. I now entrust selection affairs to you; you may take charge openly, with no need to defer."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Secretariat Director He Yan was ill. The emperor said to Xingzong: "You are well versed in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy. I now entrust selection affairs to you; take charge openly, with no need to defer."

sentences.zh: 」轉司徒左長史，復為中庶子，領前軍將軍，遷侍中。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Left in the Grand Tutor's office, again became Senior Attendant of the Heir Apparent, took concurrent command as General of the Forward Army, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to chief clerk on the left in the Grand Tutor's office, again became senior attendant of the heir apparent, took concurrent command as general of the forward army, and was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 每正言得失，無所顧憚，由是失旨。

translations.literal: He always spoke plainly of right and wrong without regard for consequences, and thereby lost imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: He always spoke plainly about right and wrong without fear of consequences, and in this way he lost the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵城為逆，事平，興宗奉旨慰勞。

translations.literal: Prince Dan of Jingling seized Guangling city in rebellion. When the affair was settled, Xingzong was ordered to offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling seized Guangling in rebellion. When the affair was settled, Xingzong was ordered to offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 州別駕范義與興宗素善，在城內同誅。

translations.literal: Provincial Registrar Fan Yi had long been on good terms with Xingzong and was executed together with others inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial registrar Fan Yi had long been on good terms with Xingzong and was executed with others inside the city.

sentences.zh: 興宗至廣陵，躬自收殯，致喪還豫章舊墓。

translations.literal: Xingzong went to Guangling, personally gathered the remains for burial, and conveyed the coffin back to the old tomb in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong went to Guangling, personally gathered Fan Yi's remains for burial, and conveyed the coffin back to the old family tomb in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甚不悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 廬陵內史周朗以正言得罪，鎖付寧州，親戚故人，無敢瞻送；

translations.literal: Zhou Lang, Interior Secretary of Luling, offended by speaking plainly and was shackled and sent to Ning Province. Kin and old friends dared not go to see him off;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang, interior secretary of Luling, offended by speaking plainly and was shackled and sent to Ning Province. Kin and old friends dared not go to see him off;

sentences.zh: 興宗在直，請急，詣朗別。

translations.literal: Xingzong was on duty, requested urgent leave, and went to bid Zhou Lang farewell.
translations.idiomatic: On duty at court, Xingzong requested urgent leave and went to bid Zhou Lang farewell.

sentences.zh: 上知尤怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of it, he was especially angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, his anger only grew.

sentences.zh: 坐屬疾多日，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was punished for belonging to the sick for many days and held his post in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for a prolonged illness and held his post in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 尋左遷司空沈慶之長史，行兗州事，還為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted to Chief Clerk under Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi, acting for Yan Province, then returned as Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to chief clerk under Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi, with acting authority over Yan Province, then returned as director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 有解士先者，告申坦昔與丞相義宣同謀。

translations.literal: A man named Xie Shixian reported that Shen Tan had once plotted together with Chancellor Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: One Xie Shixian came forward to report that Shen Tan had once plotted together with Chancellor Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 時坦已死，子令孫時作山陽郡。

translations.literal: Tan was already dead; his son Ling Sun was then serving as governor of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was already dead; his son Ling Sun was then serving as governor of Shanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 自繫廷尉。

translations.literal: He surrendered himself to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Sun turned himself in to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 興宗議曰：「若坦昔為戎首，身今尚存，累經肆眚，猶應蒙宥。

translations.literal: Xingzong judged, saying: "If Tan had once been the ringleader of the rebellion and were still alive, having passed through repeated amnesties he should still receive pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong argued: "If Tan had once been the ringleader of the rebellion and were still alive, having passed through repeated amnesties he should still receive pardon.

sentences.zh: 令孫天屬，理相為隱。

translations.literal: Ling Sun is a close blood relation; by principle one conceals for kin.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Sun is a close blood relation; by principle one conceals wrongdoing for kin.

sentences.zh: 況人亡事遠，追相誣訐，斷以禮律，義不合關。

translations.literal: Moreover, the man is dead and the affair remote; to pursue mutual slander and judge by ritual and statute—in principle this does not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the man is dead and the affair long past; to pursue mutual slander and judge by ritual and statute—in principle this does not apply.

sentences.zh: 若士先審知逆謀，當時即應聞啟，苞藏積年，發因私怨，況稱風聲路傳，實無定主，而干黷欺罔，罪合極法。

translations.literal: If Shixian truly knew of the treasonous plot, he should have reported it at once. Concealing it for years and bringing it forth from private resentment—moreover he speaks of rumors passed along the roads, with no fixed proof—yet he presumptuously deceives and misleads; his crime warrants the extreme penalty."
translations.idiomatic: If Shixian truly knew of the treasonous plot, he should have reported it at once. He concealed it for years and now brings it forth from private resentment; moreover he speaks of rumors passed along the roads, with no fixed proof—yet he presumptuously deceives and misleads. His crime warrants the extreme penalty."

sentences.zh: 」又有訟民嚴道恩等二十二人，事未洗正，敕以當訊，權繫尚方。

translations.literal: " There were also twenty-two litigants including Yan Dao'en whose cases had not yet been cleared. An edict ordered them to be interrogated and provisionally detained in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: " There were also twenty-two litigants, including Yan Dao'en, whose cases had not yet been cleared. An edict ordered them interrogated and provisionally detained in the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 興宗以訟民本在求理，故不加械，即若繫尚方，於事為苦。

translations.literal: Xingzong held that litigants seek justice by nature and therefore should not be shackled; to detain them in the Imperial Workshop would be unduly harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong held that litigants come to court seeking justice and therefore should not be shackled; to detain them in the Imperial Workshop would be unduly harsh.

sentences.zh: 又司徒前劾送武康令謝沈及郡縣尉還職司十一人，坐仲良鑄錢不禽，久已判結。

translations.literal: Again, the Grand Tutor had earlier impeached and sent eleven officials including Wukang Magistrate Xie Shen and district and county assistants, charged with failing to arrest Zhongliang for coining; the case had long been decided.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Grand Tutor had earlier impeached and sent eleven officials including Wukang magistrate Xie Shen and district and county assistants, charged with failing to arrest Zhongliang for coining; the case had long been decided.

sentences.zh: 又送郡主簿丘元敬等九人，或下疾假，或去職已久。

translations.literal: Again nine men including Commandery Registrar Qiu Yuanjing were sent up; some were on sick leave, some had left office long before.
translations.idiomatic: Again nine men including commandery registrar Qiu Yuanjing were sent up; some were on sick leave, some had left office long before.

sentences.zh: 又加執啟，事悉見從。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a firm memorial, and in all matters his views were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Again he submitted a firm memorial, and the court followed his advice in every matter.

sentences.zh: 出為東陽太守，遷安陸王子綏後軍長史、江夏內史，行郢州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Dongyang, was moved to Rear Army Chief Clerk under Prince Zishao of Anlu and Interior Secretary of Jiangxia, acting for Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Dongyang, was moved to rear army chief clerk under Prince Zishao of Anlu and interior secretary of Jiangxia, with acting authority over Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 徵還，未拜，留為左民尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned back, before he could take up appointment he was retained as Director of the Left Bureau of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back, before he could take up appointment he was retained as director of the Left Bureau of the People.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉掌吏部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時上方盛淫宴，虐侮群臣，自江夏王義恭以下，咸加穢辱，唯興宗以方直見憚，不被侵媟。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was given to lavish feasting and abused and insulted the hundred officials. From Prince Yigong of Jiangxia downward, all were subjected to foul humiliation; only Xingzong, because of his upright firmness, was feared and not molested.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was given to lavish feasting and abused and insulted the officials. From Prince Yigong of Jiangxia downward, all were subjected to foul humiliation; only Xingzong, because of his upright firmness, was feared and not molested.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射顏師伯謂議曹郎王耽之曰：「蔡尚書常免昵戲，去人實遠。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shibo said to Review Gentleman Wang Danzhi: "Director Cai is always spared intimate jesting; he is truly far removed from ordinary men."
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Secretariat Yan Shibo said to review gentleman Wang Danzhi: "Director Cai is always spared intimate jesting; he is truly far removed from ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 」耽之曰：「蔡豫章昔在相府，亦以方嚴不狎，武帝宴私之日，未嘗相召，每至官賭，常在勝朋。

translations.literal: " Danzhi said: "Cai of Yuzhang, when formerly in the chancellor's office, was also upright and stern and not familiar. On the days of Emperor Wu's private feasts he was never summoned; whenever officials gambled, he was always among the winning party."
translations.idiomatic: " Danzhi said: "Cai of Yuzhang, when formerly in the chancellor's office, was also upright and stern and kept his distance. On the days of Emperor Wu's private feasts he was never summoned; whenever officials gambled, he was always among the winning party."

sentences.zh: 蔡尚書今日可謂能負荷矣。」

translations.literal: Director Cai today may be said truly able to bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: Director Cai today may truly be said able to bear the burden."

sentences.zh: 大明末，前廢帝即位，興宗告太宰江夏王義恭，應須策文。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era, when the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, Xingzong told Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia that an accession document was required.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era, when the Deposed Former Emperor ascended the throne, Xingzong told Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia that an accession document was required.

sentences.zh: 義恭曰：「建立儲副，本為今日，復安用此。

translations.literal: Yigong said: "Establishing the heir was originally for this day—what further use is there for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said: "We established the heir precisely for this day—what further use is there for such a document?"

sentences.zh: 」興宗曰：「累朝故事，莫不皆然。

translations.literal: " Xingzong said: "The precedents of successive dynasties have all been thus.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingzong said: "The precedents of successive dynasties have all been the same.

sentences.zh: 近永初之末，營陽王即位，亦有文策，今在尚書，可檢視也。

translations.literal: Recently, at the end of Yongchu, when the Lord of Yingyang took the throne, there was also a written accession document; it is now in the Secretariat and may be examined."
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, at the close of Yongchu, when the Lord of Yingyang took the throne, there was also a written accession document; it is kept today in the Secretariat and may be consulted."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " He did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Yigong would not agree.

sentences.zh: 興宗時親奉璽綬，嗣主容色自若，了無哀貌。

translations.literal: Xingzong then personally presented the seal and cord; the new lord's countenance was at ease, with no trace of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong then personally presented the seal and cord; the new emperor's countenance was at ease, with no trace of mourning.

sentences.zh: 興宗出謂親故曰：「魯昭在戚而有嘉容，終之以釁結大臣，昭子請死。

translations.literal: Xingzong went out and said to kin and old friends: "Duke Zhao of Lu, while in mourning, wore a pleasant expression; it ended with offense against great ministers, and Zhaozi asked for death.
translations.idiomatic: As he went out, Xingzong said to kin and old friends: "Duke Zhao of Lu, while in mourning, wore a pleasant expression; it ended with offense against great ministers, and Zhaozi asked for death.

sentences.zh: 國家之禍，其在此乎。

translations.literal: The state's calamity—is it here?
translations.idiomatic: Is the state's calamity to be found here?

sentences.zh: 」時義恭錄尚書事，受遺輔政，阿衡幼主，而引身避事，政歸近習。

translations.literal: " At the time Yigong recorded Secretariat affairs, received the dying charge to assist governance, and should have steadied the young lord—yet he withdrew from affairs, and government fell to close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Yigong recorded Secretariat affairs, received the dying charge to assist governance, and should have steadied the young emperor—yet he withdrew from affairs, and government fell to close attendants.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉戴法興、中書舍人巢尚之專制朝權，威行近遠。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Upland Cavalry Dai Faxing and Secretariat Attendant Chao Shangzhi monopolized court power; their authority reached near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the upland cavalry Dai Faxing and secretariat attendant Chao Shangzhi monopolized court power; their authority reached near and far.

sentences.zh: 興宗職管九流，銓衡所寄，每至上朝，輒與令錄以下，陳欲登賢進士之意，又箴規得失，博論朝政。

translations.literal: Xingzong's office governed the nine classes and bore the weight of evaluation. At each court session he would speak with the Recorder of the Secretariat and those below, stating his intent to elevate the worthy and advance scholars, and also admonish on right and wrong, broadly discussing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's office governed the nine classes and bore the weight of evaluation. At each court session he would speak with the recorder of the Secretariat and those below, stating his intent to elevate the worthy and advance scholars, and also admonish on right and wrong, broadly discussing court affairs.

sentences.zh: 義恭素性恇橈，阿順法興，常慮失旨，聞興宗言，輒戰懼無計。

translations.literal: Yigong was by nature timid and weak, fawning on Faxing and always fearing to lose imperial favor. Hearing Xingzong's words, he would tremble in fear without resource.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was by nature timid and weak, fawning on Faxing and always fearing to lose imperial favor. Hearing Xingzong's words, he would tremble in fear, utterly at a loss.

sentences.zh: 先是大明世，奢侈無度，多所造立，賦調煩嚴，徵役過苦。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Daming era, extravagance knew no bounds; many structures were built; levies and taxes were burdensome and severe; corvée labor was excessively harsh.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era that preceded this, extravagance knew no bounds; the court built on every side; levies and taxes grew burdensome and severe; corvée labor was crushing.

sentences.zh: 至是發詔，悉皆削除，由此紫極殿南北馳道之屬，皆被毀壞。

translations.literal: At this time an edict was issued abolishing all of them; thereby the north-south imperial avenues of the Ziji Hall and the like were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was now issued abolishing all of it; the north-south imperial avenues of the Ziji Hall and the like were torn down.

sentences.zh: 自孝建以來至大明末，凡諸制度，無或存者。

translations.literal: From Xiaojian onward to the end of Daming, of all institutions none remained.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian to the end of Daming, not one of those institutions survived.

sentences.zh: 興宗於都坐慨然謂顏師伯曰：「先帝雖非盛德主，要以道始終。

translations.literal: Xingzong said with feeling at the capital session to Yan Shibo: "The late emperor, though not a ruler of overflowing virtue, nevertheless saw the Way through from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: At a capital session Xingzong said with feeling to Yan Shibo: "The late emperor, though not a ruler of overflowing virtue, nevertheless saw the Way through from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 三年無改，古典所貴。

translations.literal: Three years without change—this the classics honor.
translations.idiomatic: To leave things unchanged for three years—this the classics hold dear.

sentences.zh: 今殯宮始徹，山陵未遠，而凡諸制度興造，不論是非，一皆刊削。

translations.literal: Now the mourning palace has just been cleared and the imperial mound is not yet distant, yet all institutions and constructions, without regard to right or wrong, are entirely cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mourning palace has just been cleared and the imperial tomb is not yet distant, yet all institutions and constructions, without regard to right or wrong, are entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 雖復禪代，亦不至爾。

translations.literal: Even at a transfer of the mandate, it would not go this far.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the mandate passed from one house to another, matters did not go this far.

sentences.zh: 天下有識，當以此窺人。

translations.literal: Men of understanding in the realm will judge the man by this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of understanding throughout the realm will judge the man by this.

sentences.zh: 」師伯不能用。

translations.literal: " Shibo could not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shibo could not bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 興宗每陳選事，法興、尚之等輒點定回換，僅有在者。

translations.literal: Whenever Xingzong presented selection matters, Faxing, Shangzhi, and the like would mark and alter them in return; only a few remained as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xingzong presented selection matters, Faxing, Shangzhi, and the like would mark and alter them; only a few remained as proposed.

sentences.zh: 興宗於朝堂謂義恭及師伯曰：「主上諒闇，不親萬機，而選舉密事，多被刪改，復非公筆，亦不知是何天子意。

translations.literal: Xingzong said in the court hall to Yigong and Shibo: "The lord is in deep mourning and does not attend to the myriad affairs, yet confidential selection matters are largely deleted and altered—not even in your own hand—and one does not know whose imperial will this is."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said in the court hall to Yigong and Shibo: "The emperor is in deep mourning and does not attend to state affairs, yet confidential selection matters are largely deleted and altered—not even in your own hand—and one does not know whose imperial will this is."

sentences.zh: 」王景文、謝莊等遷授失序，興宗又欲為美選。

translations.literal: " Wang Jingwen, Xie Zhuang, and others were transferred and appointed out of order; Xingzong again wished to make fine selections.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jingwen, Xie Zhuang, and others had been transferred and appointed out of order; Xingzong again wished to make worthy selections.

sentences.zh: 時薛安都為散騎常侍、征虜將軍、太子左率，殷常為中庶子。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Andu was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Left Leader of the Heir Apparent; Yin Chang was Senior Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xue Andu was regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the barbarians, and left leader of the heir apparent; Yin Chang was senior attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 興宗先選安都為左衛將軍，常侍如故；

translations.literal: Xingzong first selected Andu as General of the Left Guard, with regular attendant unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong first selected Andu as general of the left guard, with regular attendant unchanged;

sentences.zh: 殷常為黃門，領校。

translations.literal: Yin Chang as Yellow Gate, concurrently colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chang as yellow gate gentleman, concurrently colonel.

sentences.zh: 太宰嫌安都為多，欲單為左衛，興宗曰：「率衛相去，唯阿之間。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor thought Andu was given too much and wished to make him only Left Guard. Xingzong said: "Between leader and guard the distance is only a span.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor thought Andu was given too much and wished to make him only left guard. Xingzong said: "Between leader and guard the distance is only a span.

sentences.zh: 且已失征虜，非乃超越，復奪常侍，頓為降貶。

translations.literal: Moreover he has already lost Pacifying the Barbarians—this is not advancement—and to take away regular attendant as well is suddenly a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he has already lost general who pacifies the barbarians—this is not advancement—and to take away regular attendant as well is suddenly a demotion.

sentences.zh: 若謂安都晚達微人，本宜裁抑，令名器不輕，宜有貫序。

translations.literal: If one holds that Andu, a man of late attainment and humble origin, should be restrained so that titles are not lightly given, there should still be a consistent order.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that Andu, having risen late from humble origins, ought to be held back so that titles are not lightly bestowed, there should still be a consistent order.

sentences.zh: 謹依選體，非私安都。

translations.literal: I respectfully follow the norms of selection; this is not favoritism for Andu.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully follow the norms of selection; this is not private favor for Andu.

sentences.zh: 」義恭曰：「若宮官宜加超授者，殷常便應侍中，那得為黃門而已。

translations.literal: " Yigong said: "If palace officials should receive extraordinary promotion, Yin Chang ought to be Palace Attendant—how can he be only Yellow Gate?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yigong said: "If palace officials should receive extraordinary promotion, Yin Chang ought to be palace attendant—how can he be only yellow gate gentleman?"

sentences.zh: 」興宗又曰：「中庶、侍中，相去實遠。

translations.literal: " Xingzong again said: "Between senior attendant and palace attendant the distance is truly great.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingzong added: "Between senior attendant and palace attendant the distance is truly great.

sentences.zh: 且安都作率十年，殷恆中庶百日，今又領校，不為少也。

translations.literal: Moreover Andu has served as leader for ten years; Yin Heng has been senior attendant for a hundred days; now he also holds colonel—this is not little."
translations.idiomatic: Andu has led for ten years; Yin Heng has been senior attendant for a hundred days; now he also holds colonel—surely that is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 」使選令史顏禕之、薛慶先等往復論執，義恭然後署案。

translations.literal: " He had selection clerks Yan Yizhi, Xue Qingxian, and others argue back and forth; only then did Yigong sign the document.
translations.idiomatic: " He had selection clerks Yan Yizhi, Xue Qingxian, and others debate back and forth; only then did Yigong sign the document.

sentences.zh: 既中旨以安都為右衛，加給事中，由是大忤義恭及法興等，出興宗吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When an imperial order then made Andu Right Guard and added Attendant to the Affairs of the Masters, Xingzong thereby greatly offended Yigong, Faxing, and the rest, and was sent out as Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial order then made Andu right guard and added attendant to the affairs of the masters, Xingzong thereby greatly offended Yigong, Faxing, and the rest, and was sent out as governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 固辭郡，執政愈怒，又轉為新安王子鸞撫軍司馬、輔國將軍、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the commandery; the ruling faction grew angrier and transferred him to Pacifying Army Marshal under Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, Aid-the-State General, and Governor of Southern Donghai, acting for Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the commandery; the ruling faction grew angrier and transferred him to pacifying army marshal under Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, aid-the-state general, and governor of Southern Donghai, with acting authority over Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又不拜，苦求益州。

translations.literal: Again he did not accept; he urgently requested Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He again refused the appointment and pressed urgently for Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 義恭於是大怒，上表曰：「臣聞慎節言語，《大易》有規，銓序九流，無取裁囗。

translations.literal: Yigong was then greatly angered and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that one must be careful in speech; the Great Changes has regulations on this. In ordering the nine classes, one should not take arbitrary judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was then furious and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that one must be careful in speech; the Book of Changes has regulations on this. In ordering the nine classes, one should not take arbitrary judgment.

sentences.zh: 若乃結黨連群，譏訴互起，街談巷議，罔顧聽聞，乃撤實憲制所宜禁經之巨蠹。

translations.literal: If men form factions and link groups, slander and accusations rise against one another, and street and lane talk disregards what reaches the ears, this is truly the great pest that statutes and institutions ought to forbid.
translations.idiomatic: If men form factions and link groups, slander and accusations rise against one another, and street talk disregards what reaches the throne, this is truly the great pest that law and institutions ought to forbid.

sentences.zh: 侍中秘書監臣彧自表父疾，必求侍養，聖旨矜體，特順所陳，改授臣府元僚，兼帶軍郡。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat Yu submitted himself that his father was ill and he must request to attend and nurture him. The sacred edict showed compassion and specially granted his request, changing his appointment to a chief aide in your servant's office, concurrently holding army and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant and director of the Secretariat Yu submitted that his father was ill and he must attend him. The imperial edict showed compassion and granted his request, changing his appointment to a chief aide in your servant's office, concurrently holding army and commandery posts.

sentences.zh: 雖臣駑劣，府任非輕，准之前人，不為屈後。

translations.literal: Although your servant is mediocre, the office of the prince's establishment is not light; measured against predecessors, one should not be placed lower.
translations.idiomatic: Although your servant is mediocre, the prince's establishment is not a light post; measured against predecessors, one should not be placed lower.

sentences.zh: 京郡本以為祿，不計戶之少多，遇缺便用，無關高下。

translations.literal: The capital commandery was originally for salary, without regard to the number of households; when a vacancy arose it was used, unrelated to rank high or low.
translations.idiomatic: The capital commandery was originally for salary, without regard to the number of households; when a vacancy arose it was filled, unrelated to rank high or low.

sentences.zh: 撫軍長史莊滯府累朝，每陳危苦，內職外守，稱未堪依。

translations.literal: Pacifying Army Chief Clerk Zhuang lingered in the establishment for many reigns, repeatedly stating hardship; holding inner office and outer governorship, he said he could not bear both.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying army chief clerk Zhuang lingered in the establishment for many reigns, repeatedly stating hardship; holding inner office and outer governorship, he said he could not bear both.

sentences.zh: 唯王球昔比，賜以優養，恩慈之厚，不近於薄。

translations.literal: Only Wang Qiu in former times was granted generous maintenance; the thickness of grace and kindness was not close to meager.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Qiu in former times was granted generous maintenance; the grace shown was far from meager.

sentences.zh: 前新除吳郡太守興宗，前居選曹，多不平允，鴻渥含宥，恕其不閑，改任大都，寵均阿輔，仍苦請益州，雅違成命。

translations.literal: The former newly appointed Governor of Wu Xingzong, when previously in the selection office, was often unfair; the great favor included pardon, forgiving his lack of skill, and changed him to a great commandery with favor equal to a chief aide—yet he still urgently requested Yi Province, plainly defying the settled command.
translations.idiomatic: The former newly appointed governor of Wu Xingzong, when previously in the selection office, was often unfair; the court included him in pardon, forgiving his lack of skill, and changed him to a great commandery with favor equal to a chief aide—yet he still urgently requested Yi Province, plainly defying the settled command.

sentences.zh: 伏尋揚州刺史子尚、吳興太守休若，並國之茂戚，魯、衛攸在，猶牧守東山，竭誠撫蒞，而辭擇適情，起自庶族，逮佐北藩，尤無欣荷。

translations.literal: Reflecting on Governor of Yangzhou Zishang and Governor of Wuxing Xiuruo, both eminent kin of the state, like Lu and Wei still present, yet they pasture and guard the eastern hills with full sincerity—while he picks and chooses to suit his mood, rising from the common clans, reaching to aide the northern frontier, especially without joyful acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on Governor of Yangzhou Zishang and Governor of Wuxing Xiuruo, both eminent kin of the state, like Lu and Wei still present, yet they govern the eastern regions with full sincerity—while he picks and chooses to suit his mood, rising from the common clans, reaching to aide the northern frontier, especially without joyful acceptance.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞永，昔歲餘愆，從恩今授，光祿勳臣淹，雖曰代臣，累經降黜，後效未申，以何取進。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yong had remaining faults from former years yet is appointed by grace today; Minister of the Imperial Household Chen Yan, though called a replacement minister, has been repeatedly demoted; later merit not yet shown—on what basis advance?
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Yong had remaining faults from former years yet is appointed by grace today; minister of the imperial household Chen Yan, though called a replacement minister, has been repeatedly demoted; later merit not yet shown—on what basis should he advance?

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史孔覬，前除右衛，尋徙今職，回換之宜，不為乃少。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk on the Left in the Grand Tutor's office Kong Gu, previously appointed Right Guard and soon moved to the present post—the fitness of exchange is not that he received too little.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk on the left in the Grand Tutor's office Kong Gu, previously appointed right guard and soon moved to the present post—the fitness of the exchange is not that he received too little.

sentences.zh: 竊外談謂彧等咸為失分，又聞興宗躬自怨懟，與尚書右僕射師伯疏，辭旨甚苦。

translations.literal: Privately outside talk says Yu and the rest all lost proper measure; I also hear Xingzong personally resentful, writing to Vice Director of the Secretariat Shibo with very bitter wording.
translations.idiomatic: Privately it is said Yu and the rest all lost proper measure; I also hear Xingzong personally resentful, writing to vice director of the Secretariat Shibo with very bitter wording.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不見，所聞不虛。

translations.literal: Your servant has not seen it, but what is heard is not false.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has not seen it himself, but what is reported is not false.

sentences.zh: 臣以凡才，不應機務，謬自幸會，受任三朝，進無古人興賢之美，退無在下獻替之績，致茲紛紜，伏增慚悚。

translations.literal: Your servant, with ordinary talent, should not handle urgent affairs; wrongly favored by chance, entrusted across three reigns, advancing without the ancients' beauty of raising the worthy, retreating without the subordinates' record of offering corrections—bringing on this turmoil, I prostrate myself in increased shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, with ordinary talent, should not handle urgent affairs; wrongly favored by chance, entrusted across three reigns, advancing without the ancients' beauty of raising the worthy, retreating without subordinates' record of offering corrections—bringing on this turmoil, I prostrate myself in increased shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 然此源不塞，此風弗變，將虧正道，塵穢盛猷。

translations.literal: Yet if this source is not stopped and this wind not changed, the correct Way will be impaired and the great design befouled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless this source is stopped and this wind changed, the correct Way will be impaired and the great design befouled.

sentences.zh: 伏顧聖德，賜垂覽察。

translations.literal: I humbly look to Your sacred virtue and beg that You deign to examine and consider.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly look to Your sacred virtue and beg that You deign to examine the matter.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「太宰表如此，省以憮然。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Grand Preceptor's memorial is as above; upon reading it I am deeply distressed."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict responded: "The Grand Preceptor's memorial is as stated above; upon reviewing it I am deeply troubled."

sentences.zh: 朕恭承洪緒，思弘盛烈，而在朝倰競，驅扇成風，將何以式揚先德，克隆至化。

translations.literal: I respectfully inherit the great succession and think to spread glorious achievements, yet disorderly rivalry in court drives and fans faction until it becomes the prevailing wind—how then shall I extol the virtue of our forebears and reproduce the highest transformation?
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully inherit the great succession and mean to spread our glorious achievements, yet disorderly rivalry at court drives faction until it becomes the prevailing wind—how then can I extol the virtue of our forebears and bring about the highest transformation?

sentences.zh: 公體國情深，保釐攸託，便可付外詳議。」

translations.literal: Your Grace's concern for the state runs deep, and the charge of safeguarding and ordering the realm is entrusted to you; this may therefore be referred outward for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace's concern for the state runs deep, and the charge of safeguarding and ordering the realm is entrusted to you; let this be referred outward for detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 義恭因使尚書令柳元景奏曰：「臣義恭表、詔書如右。

translations.literal: Yigong thereupon had the Minister of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing memorialize, saying: "Your servant Yigong's memorial and the edict are as at right."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong thereupon had the Minister of the Secretariat Liu Yuanjing submit a memorial saying: "Your servant Yigong's memorial and the edict are as at right."

sentences.zh: 攝曹辨核尚書袁愍孫牒：『此月十七日，詣僕射顏師伯，語次，因及尚書蔡興宗有書固辭今授，仍出疏見示，乃者數紙，不意悉何所道，緣此因及朝士。

translations.literal: The acting bureau investigated and verified Minister Yuan Minsun's report: 'On the seventeenth of this month I went to Vice Director Yan Shibo; in the course of conversation the matter arose of Minister Cai Xingzong's letter firmly declining the present appointment, and he produced the memorial for me to see—several sheets—and I did not expect what he was saying in full; because of this the talk turned to court officials.'
translations.idiomatic: The acting bureau investigated and verified Minister Yuan Minsun's report: 'On the seventeenth of this month I went to Vice Director Yan Shibo; in conversation the matter arose of Minister Cai Xingzong's letter firmly declining the present appointment, and he produced the memorial for me to see—several sheets—and I did not expect everything he was saying; because of this the talk turned to court officials.'

sentences.zh: 當今聖世，不可使人以為少。

translations.literal: In the present sagely age, one must not let people think the appointments are too few.
translations.idiomatic: In this sagely age, one must not let people think the appointments are too few.

sentences.zh: 今牒。

translations.literal: Here is the report.
translations.idiomatic: The report follows.

sentences.zh: 』數之，朝廷處之實得所，臣等亦自謂得分，常多在門，袁愍孫無或措多，而愚意欲啟更量出內之宜，芻蕘管見，願在聞徹。

translations.literal: Counting them, the court's handling was in fact appropriate; we also consider ourselves to have obtained our share—Chang Duo is often at the gate, and Yuan Minsun had nothing further to add—but my humble intent is to submit a request to reconsider what is appropriate for appointments from within, offering crude grass and a narrow-tube view, in hope that it will be heard and understood.
translations.idiomatic: Counting them, the court's handling was in fact appropriate; we also consider ourselves to have obtained our share—Chang Duo is often at the gate, and Yuan Minsun had nothing further to add—but my humble intent is to submit a request to reconsider what is appropriate for appointments from within, offering a crude and narrow view in hope that it will be heard and understood.

sentences.zh: 選令史宣傳密事，故因附上聞，亦外人言此。

translations.literal: The selection clerks spread confidential matters, and so I attach this for transmission upward; outsiders also speak of this.
