translations.idiomatic: The selection clerks spread confidential matters, and so I attach this for transmission upward; outsiders speak of this as well.

sentences.zh: 今薛慶先列：『今月十八日，往尚書袁愍孫論選事。

translations.literal: Now Xue Qingxian states: 'On the eighteenth of this month I went to Minister Yuan Minsun to discuss selection affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qingxian now states: 'On the eighteenth of this month I went to Minister Yuan Minsun to discuss selection affairs.'

sentences.zh: 愍孫云，昨詣顏僕射，出蔡尚書疏見示，言辭甚苦。

translations.literal: Minsun said that yesterday he went to Vice Director Yan and was shown Minister Cai's memorial; the language was very bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Minsun said that yesterday he called on Vice Director Yan, who showed him Minister Cai's memorial; the language was very bitter.

sentences.zh: 又云所得亦少。

translations.literal: He also said that what he obtained was likewise too little.
translations.idiomatic: He also complained that what he obtained was likewise too little.

sentences.zh: 主上踐阼始爾，朝士有此人不多，物議謂應美用，乃更恨少，使咨事便啟錄公。

translations.literal: The sovereign has only just ascended the throne; among court officials there are not many men of this caliber, and public opinion holds they ought to be well employed—yet he complained all the more that there were too few, and had the advisory office immediately submit a record to the Duke.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign has only just ascended the throne; men of this caliber are scarce at court, and public opinion holds they ought to be well employed—yet he complained all the more that there were too few, and had the advisory office immediately submit a record to the Duke.

sentences.zh: 又謝莊囗時未老，其疾以轉差，今居此任，復為非宜，謂宜中書令才望為允。

translations.literal: He also said that Xie Zhuang, though not yet old, had an illness that was turning for the better, and that holding this post was again unsuitable; he held that a man of talent and standing as Director of the Secretariat would be appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Xie Zhuang, though not yet old, had an illness that was turning for the better, and that holding this post was again unsuitable; he held that a man of talent and standing ought to serve as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又孔覬南士之美，所歷已多，近頻授即復回改，於理為屈，門下無人，此是名選。

translations.literal: He also said that Kong Gu, a fine man of the south, had already held many posts; recently, after frequent appointments he was again transferred and changed—a logical injustice—and that with no one in the Secretariat, this was a notable selection.
translations.idiomatic: He also observed that Kong Gu, a fine man of the south, had already held many posts; recently, after repeated appointments he was transferred once more—a logical injustice—and with no one in the Secretariat, this was a notable selection.

sentences.zh: 又張永人地可論，其去歲愆戾，非為深罪，依其望復門下一人。

translations.literal: He also said that Zhang Yong's personal standing was worth considering; his offense of last year, though rebellious, was not a grave crime, and according to his standing he should again receive one post in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Zhang Yong's personal standing was worth considering; his offense of last year, though rebellious, was not a grave crime, and by his standing he should again receive one post in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張淹昔忝南下，預同休戚，雖屢經愆黜，事亦已久，謂應秘書監。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan once had the honor of going south and shared in weal and woe; though he had repeatedly been punished and demoted, that was long ago, and he held that Yan should be made Director of the Secretariat for Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He said Zhang Yan once had the honor of going south and shared in weal and woe; though he had repeatedly been punished and demoted, that was long ago, and Yan ought to be made Director of the Secretariat for Compilation.

sentences.zh: 』帶授興宗手跡數紙，文翰炳然，事證明白，不假核辨。

translations.literal: Attached were several sheets in Cai Xingzong's own hand; the writing was clear and the evidence plain, requiring no further verification.
translations.idiomatic: Enclosed were several sheets in Cai Xingzong's own hand; the writing was clear and the evidence plain, with no need for further verification.

sentences.zh: 愍孫任居官人，職掌銓裁，若有未允，則宜顯言，而私加許與，自相選署，託云物論，終成虛詭，隱末出端，還為矛楯。

translations.literal: Minsun holds the post of a minister and his duty is to judge selection; if something is not acceptable, he ought to speak openly, yet he privately gave approval and made mutual appointments, claiming public opinion—only to produce falsehood in the end, hiding the source while the tail appeared, and thus creating contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Minsun holds a ministerial post and his duty is to judge selection; if something is not acceptable, he ought to speak openly, yet he privately gave approval and made mutual appointments, claiming public opinion—only to produce falsehood in the end, hiding the source while the tail appeared, and thus creating contradiction.

sentences.zh: 臣聞九官成讓，虞風垂則，誹主怨時，漢罪夙斷。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the Nine Ministers completed their mutual yielding, the virtue of Yu set the standard, and that slandering one's lord and resenting the times was long ago judged a crime under Han law.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when the Nine Ministers yielded their posts to one another, the virtue of Yu became the standard, and that to slander one's lord and resent the times was long ago judged a crime under Han law.

sentences.zh: 況義為身發，言謗朝序，亂辟害政，混穢大猷，紛紜彰謬，上延詔旨，不有霜准，軌憲斯淪。

translations.literal: How much more when righteousness is invoked for private ends, speech slanders the court order, disorderly punishments harm governance, and the great design is befouled—confusion makes error manifest and extends upward to the edict; without frost-like standard, the norms and statutes will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when righteousness is invoked for private ends, speech slanders the court order, disorderly punishments harm governance, and the great design is befouled—confusion makes error manifest and extends upward to the edict; without a frost-like standard, the norms and statutes will collapse.

sentences.zh: 請解興宗新附官，須事御，收付廷尉法獄治罪，免愍孫所居官。

translations.literal: We request that Cai Xingzong's newly granted office be removed, that the matter await imperial handling, that he be taken and handed over to the Court of Justice for punishment according to law, and that Minsun be removed from the office he holds.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Cai Xingzong's newly granted office be removed, that the matter await imperial decision, that he be taken and handed over to the Court of Justice for legal punishment, and that Minsun be dismissed from the office he holds.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「興宗首亂朝典，允當明憲，以其昔經近侍，未忍盡法，可令思愆遠封。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Cai Xingzong was foremost in disrupting court norms and fully deserves the clear penalty of law; because he once served in close attendance, We cannot bear to apply the full measure of punishment—let him reflect on his faults from afar in exile."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Cai Xingzong was foremost in disrupting court norms and fully deserves the clear penalty of the law; because he once served in close attendance, We cannot bear to apply the full measure of punishment—let him reflect on his faults from afar in exile."

sentences.zh: 愍孫竊評自己，委咎物議，可以子領職。」

translations.literal: Minsun privately judged on his own behalf and shifted blame to public opinion; his son may take over the post."
translations.idiomatic: Minsun had privately judged on his own behalf and shifted blame to public opinion; his son may take over the post."

sentences.zh: 除興宗新昌太守，郡屬交州。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong was appointed Administrator of Xinchang, a commandery subordinate to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong was made Administrator of Xinchang, a commandery subordinate to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷莫不嗟駭。

translations.literal: Everyone at court sighed and was appalled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court sighed in shock.

sentences.zh: 先是，興宗納何后寺尼智妃為妾，姿貌甚美，有名京師，迎車已去，而師伯密遣人誘之，潛往載取，興宗迎人不覺。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cai Xingzong had taken as a concubine the nun Zhifei of Empress He's temple; her appearance was very beautiful and she was famous in the capital. The welcoming carriage had already departed when Yan Shibo secretly sent men to entice her, went secretly to seize and carry her off, and Cai Xingzong's welcoming party did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cai Xingzong had taken as a concubine the nun Zhifei of Empress He's temple; her beauty was renowned in the capital. The welcoming carriage had already departed when Yan Shibo secretly sent men to entice her, seized her in secret, and carried her off—Cai Xingzong's welcoming party never noticed.

sentences.zh: 及興宗被徙，論者並云由師伯，師伯甚病之。

translations.literal: When Cai Xingzong was banished, commentators all said it was because of Yan Shibo, and Yan Shibo was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Xingzong was banished, commentators all attributed it to Yan Shibo, and Shibo was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 法興等既不欲以徙大臣為名，師伯又欲止息物議，由此停行。

translations.literal: Dai Faxiang and the others neither wished to be known for banishing a great minister, nor did Yan Shibo wish to quiet public talk; for this reason the transfer was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Faxiang and the others did not wish to be known for banishing a great minister, and Shibo also wanted to quiet public talk; for this reason the transfer was halted.

sentences.zh: 頃之，法興見殺，尚之被繫，義恭、師伯誅，復起興宗為臨海王子頊前軍長史、輔國將軍、南郡太守，行荊州事，不行。

translations.literal: Before long Dai Faxiang was killed, Chao Shangzhi was imprisoned, and Yigong and Yan Shibo were executed; Cai Xingzong was again raised up as Chief Clerk of the Vanguard for Liu Zixu, Prince of Linhai, General Who Supports the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, acting as governor of Jingzhou—but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Faxiang was killed, Shangzhi was imprisoned, and Yigong and Shibo were executed; Xingzong was again raised up as Chief Clerk of the Vanguard for Liu Zixu, Prince of Linhai, General Who Supports the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, acting as governor of Jingzhou—but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 時前廢帝兇暴，興宗外甥袁顗為雍州刺史，勸興宗行，曰：「朝廷形勢，人所共見，在內大臣，朝夕難保。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Former Emperor was violent and cruel; Cai Xingzong's nephew Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou and urged Cai Xingzong to go, saying: "The situation at court is plain for all to see; the great ministers within cannot be assured of their lives from one morning to the next."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Deposed Former Emperor was violent and cruel; Xingzong's nephew Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou and urged him to leave, saying: "The situation at court is plain for all to see; the great ministers within cannot be assured of their lives from one morning to the next."

sentences.zh: 舅今出居陝西，為八州行事，顗在襄、沔，地勝兵強，去江陵咫尺，水陸通便。

translations.literal: Uncle, you would now go out to dwell west of the Shan passes and act as governor of eight provinces; Yan is at Xiang and Mian, where the terrain is superior and the troops strong, only a short distance from Jiangling, with easy access by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you would now go out to dwell west of the Shan passes and govern eight provinces; I am at Xiang and Mian, where the terrain is superior and the troops strong, only a short distance from Jiangling, with easy access by land and water.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷有事，可共立桓、文之功，豈與受制兇狂，禍難不測，同年而語乎。

translations.literal: If something happens at court, together we could establish achievements like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen—how can that be spoken of in the same breath as submitting to a violent madman, with disaster impossible to foretell?
translations.idiomatic: If trouble comes at court, together we could achieve what Duke Huan and Duke Wen achieved—how can that be compared with submitting to a violent madman, with disaster impossible to foretell?

sentences.zh: 今不去虎口，而守此危逼，後求復出，豈得哉！

translations.literal: If you do not leave the tiger's maw now but remain in this perilous confinement, how will you ever be able to get out later!
translations.idiomatic: If you do not leave the tiger's maw now but remain in this perilous confinement, how will you ever get out later!

sentences.zh: 」興宗曰：「吾素門平進，與主上甚疏，未容有患。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "My family has always advanced by plain merit; I am very distant from the sovereign and am unlikely to meet with trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "My family has always advanced by plain merit; I am very distant from the sovereign and am unlikely to meet with trouble."

sentences.zh: 宮省內外，人不自保，會應有變。

translations.literal: Within and without the palace, no one can protect himself; there will surely be a change.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace, no one can protect himself; change is sure to come.

sentences.zh: 若內難得弭，外釁未必可量。

translations.literal: If internal trouble can be quelled, external disturbances may not necessarily be measurable.
translations.idiomatic: If internal trouble can be quelled, external disturbances may still be beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 汝欲在外求全，我欲居內免禍，各行所見，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: You wish to seek safety abroad; I wish to dwell within and avoid disaster—each acting according to his view—is that not also good?
translations.idiomatic: You wish to seek safety abroad; I wish to stay within and avoid disaster—each acting on his own judgment—is that not also well?

sentences.zh: 」時京城危懼，衣冠咸欲遠徙，後皆流離外難，百不一存。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was fearful and alarmed; officials and gentry all wished to flee far away, and afterward they were all scattered in external calamity—not one in a hundred survived.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was then fearful and alarmed; officials and gentry all wished to flee far away, and afterward they were scattered in external calamity—not one in a hundred survived.

sentences.zh: 重除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Minister of the Secretariat for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Once more he was appointed to head the Secretariat for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太尉沈慶之深慮危禍，閉門不通賓客，嘗遣左右范羨詣興宗屬事。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Shen Qingzhi deeply feared disaster and closed his gates to visitors; he once sent his attendant Fan Xian to Cai Xingzong on a matter of business.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Shen Qingzhi lived in deep fear of disaster and closed his gates to visitors; he once sent his attendant Fan Xian to Xingzong on business.

sentences.zh: 興宗謂羨曰：「公閉門絕客，以避悠悠請託耳，身非有求，何為見拒。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said to Fan Xian: "The Duke closes his gates and cuts off guests to avoid idle requests—that is all; I am not here with a request—why am I refused?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said to Fan Xian: "The Duke shuts his gates and turns away guests to avoid idle requests—that is all; I come without a request—why am I refused?"

sentences.zh: 」還造慶之，慶之遣羨報命，要興宗令往。

translations.literal: Fan Xian returned to Shen Qingzhi; Shen Qingzhi sent Fan Xian back with a reply and asked that Cai Xingzong come.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xian returned to Qingzhi; Qingzhi sent him back with a reply and asked that Xingzong come in person.

sentences.zh: 興宗因說之曰：「先帝雖無功於天下，要能定平凶逆，在位十一年，以道晏駕。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong thereupon urged him, saying: "The late Emperor Xiaowu, though he achieved no great merit for the realm, was yet able to settle and pacify violent rebels; he reigned eleven years and departed this life in accordance with the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong thereupon urged him: "The late Emperor Xiaowu, though he won no great merit for the realm, was yet able to settle and pacify violent rebels; he reigned eleven years and departed in accordance with the Way."

sentences.zh: 主上紹臨，四海清謐，即位正是舉止違衷，小小得失耳，亦謂春秋尚富，進德可期。

translations.literal: The sovereign succeeded him; the four seas were tranquil; at his accession it was merely that his conduct departed from what was fitting—small faults and lapses—and one also thought his years were still plentiful and moral progress could be expected.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign succeeded him; the four seas were tranquil; at his accession it was merely that his conduct departed from what was fitting—small faults and lapses—and people still thought his years were plentiful and moral progress could be expected.

sentences.zh: 而比者所行，人倫道盡。

translations.literal: But what he has done of late exhausts the way of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: But what he has done of late exhausts every bond of human relations.

sentences.zh: 今所忌憚，唯在於公；

translations.literal: What he now fears and dreads is you alone;
translations.idiomatic: You alone are what he now fears and dreads;

sentences.zh: 百姓喁喁，無復假息之望，所冀正在公一人而已。

translations.literal: the common people murmur and have no hope of respite; what they look to rests on you alone.
translations.idiomatic: the common people murmur and have no hope of respite; their hopes rest on you alone.

sentences.zh: 若復坐視成敗者，非唯身禍不測，四海重責，將有所歸。

translations.literal: If you again sit and watch success or failure, not only will personal disaster be impossible to foretell—the heavy responsibility of the realm will fall upon someone.
translations.idiomatic: If you again sit and watch whether things succeed or fail, not only will personal disaster be impossible to foretell—the heavy responsibility of the realm will fall on someone.

sentences.zh: 公威名素著，天下所服，今舉朝遑遑，人人危怖，指麾之日，誰不景從；

translations.literal: Your prestige and name have long been established and the realm submits to you; now the whole court is alarmed and every man is in dread—on the day you give the command, who would not follow in admiration;
translations.idiomatic: Your prestige has stood firm for years and the realm submits to you; now the whole court is alarmed and every man lives in dread—when you give the command, who would not follow with admiration;

sentences.zh: 如其不斷，旦暮禍及。

translations.literal: if you do not decide, disaster will come before long.
translations.idiomatic: unless you decide now, disaster will come at any moment.

sentences.zh: 僕者昔佐貴府，蒙眷異常，故敢盡言，願公思為其計。

translations.literal: Your servant once served in your noble household and received extraordinary favor; therefore I dare speak fully and beg you to think and plan accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: I once served in your noble household and received extraordinary favor; therefore I dare speak plainly and beg you to think and plan accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「僕皆前慮不復自保，但盡忠奉國，始終以之，正當委天任命耳。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi said: "I too have lately feared I could no longer protect myself, but to serve the state with full loyalty from beginning to end—that is my course; I should simply entrust myself to Heaven and accept my fate."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said: "I too have lately feared I could no longer protect myself, but to serve the state with full loyalty from beginning to end—that is my course; I should simply entrust myself to Heaven and accept my fate."

sentences.zh: 加老罷私門，兵力頓闕，雖有其意，事亦無從。

translations.literal: Moreover I am old and retired to my household, and my military strength is suddenly depleted; though I have the intent, there is no way to act on it.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I am old and retired to my home, and my military strength has suddenly dwindled; though I have the intent, there is no way to act on it.

sentences.zh: 」興宗曰：「當今懷謀思奮者，非要富貴，求功賞，各欲免死朝夕耳。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "Those who now harbor plans and think to rise up do not seek wealth and rank or merit and reward—they each wish only to escape death from one morning to the next."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "Those who now harbor plans and think to rise up do not seek wealth and rank or merit and reward—they each wish only to escape death from one morning to the next."

sentences.zh: 殿內將帥，正聽外間消息，若一人唱首，則俯仰可定。

translations.literal: The generals within the palace halls are just waiting for news from outside; if one man takes the lead, the matter can be settled in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: The generals within the palace halls are only waiting for word from outside; if one man takes the lead, the whole affair can be settled in an instant.

sentences.zh: 況公威風先著，統戎累朝，諸舊部曲，布在宮省，宋越、譚金之徒，出公宇下，並受生成；

translations.literal: Moreover your commanding presence was established long ago and you have commanded armies across several reigns; your old retainers are spread through the palace offices—men like Song Yue and Tan Jin came from under your roof and all received life from you;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your commanding presence was established long ago and you have commanded armies across several reigns; your old retainers are spread through the palace offices—men like Song Yue and Tan Jin came from under your roof and all owe you their lives;

sentences.zh: 攸之、恩仁，公家口子弟耳，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: Youzhi and Enren are household dependents and younger kinsmen of your family—who would dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and Enren are dependents and younger kinsmen of your household—who would dare refuse to follow?

sentences.zh: 且公門徒義附，並三吳勇士，宅內奴僮，人有數百。

translations.literal: Moreover your followers and sworn adherents are all warriors of the Three Wu regions, and the slaves and servants within your residence number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Your followers and sworn adherents are all warriors of the Three Wu regions, and the slaves and servants in your residence number in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 陸攸之今入東討賊，又大送鎧仗，在青溪未發。

translations.literal: Lu Youzhi is now entering the east to attack bandits and has also sent a large shipment of armor and weapons, which is at Qingxi and has not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi is now marching east to attack bandits and has also sent a large shipment of armor and weapons, now at Qingxi and not yet departed.

sentences.zh: 攸之公之鄉人，驍勇有膽力，取其器仗，以配衣宇下，使攸之率以前驅，天下之事定矣。

translations.literal: Youzhi is a townsman of your native place, fierce and brave with daring strength; take his weapons and armor and equip the retainers under your roof, have Youzhi lead them as vanguard, and the affairs of the realm will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi is a townsman of your native place, fierce and brave; take his weapons and armor, equip the men under your roof, put Youzhi at their head as vanguard, and the affairs of the realm will be settled.

sentences.zh: 僕在尚書中，自當率百僚案前世故事，更簡賢明，以奉社稷。

translations.literal: Your servant, in the Secretariat, would himself lead the hundred officials according to precedents of former ages, select anew the worthy and enlightened, and serve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, in the Secretariat, would lead the hundred officials according to precedents of former ages, select anew the worthy and enlightened, and serve the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲罪不加民，昌邑虐不及下，伊尹、霍光猶成大事，況今蒼生窘急，禍百往代乎。

translations.literal: Formerly Taijia's crimes did not reach the people, and Changyi's cruelty did not extend to the lower ranks—yet Yi Yin and Huo Guang still accomplished great deeds; how much more now, when the common people are in dire straits and the calamity exceeds that of former ages?
translations.idiomatic: In the past Taijia's crimes did not reach the people, and Changyi's cruelty did not extend to the lower ranks—yet Yi Yin and Huo Guang still accomplished great deeds. How much more now, when the common people are in dire straits and the calamity exceeds anything of former ages?

sentences.zh: 又朝廷諸所行造，民間皆云公悉豫之。

translations.literal: Moreover everything the court has done and built—the common people all say that you had a full part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for everything the court has done and built, the common people say you had a full hand in it.

sentences.zh: 今若沈疑不決，當有先公起事者，公亦不免附從之禍。

translations.literal: If you now sink in doubt and do not decide, there will be someone who rises up before you—and you too will not escape the disaster of being forced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: If you now sink in doubt and do not decide, someone will rise up before you—and you too will not escape the disaster of being forced to follow.

sentences.zh: 車駕屢幸貴第，醉酣彌留，又聞屏左右獨入閣內，此萬世一時，機不可失。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage has repeatedly visited your noble residence; he stays long in drunken revelry, and I have heard that he dismisses his attendants and enters the inner chamber alone—this is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations moment; the opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage has repeatedly come to your noble residence; he lingers long in drunken revelry, and I have heard that he dismisses his attendants and enters the inner chamber alone—a moment that comes once in ten thousand generations; the opportunity must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 僕荷眷深重，故吐去梯之言，宜詳其禍福。

translations.literal: Your servant bears deep favor and therefore speaks words after removing the ladder; you should weigh the blessings and disasters carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I bear your deep favor and therefore speak words after removing the ladder; you should weigh the blessings and disasters with care.

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「深感君無已。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi said: "I am deeply moved by your unceasing concern."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said: "I am deeply moved by your unceasing concern."

sentences.zh: 意此事大，非僕所能行，事至故當抱忠以沒耳。

translations.literal: I consider this matter great and not something your servant can undertake; when the matter comes I shall simply embrace loyalty and perish.
translations.idiomatic: I consider this matter great and not something your servant can undertake; when the moment comes I shall simply embrace loyalty and perish.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，慶之果以見忌致禍。

translations.literal: Before long Shen Qingzhi indeed met with disaster because he was regarded with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qingzhi indeed met with disaster because he was regarded with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 時領軍王玄謨大將有威名，邑里訛言云已見誅，市道喧擾。

translations.literal: At that time the Commandant of the Guards Wang Xuanymou was a great general with a formidable reputation; false rumors in the neighborhoods said he had already been executed, and the markets and streets were in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Commandant of the Guards Wang Xuanymou was a great general with a formidable reputation; false rumors in the neighborhoods said he had already been executed, and the markets and streets were in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 玄謨典籤包法榮者，家在東陽，興宗故郡民也，為玄謨所信，見使至，興宗因謂曰：「領軍殊當憂懼。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanymou's registrar Bao Farong was a native of Dongyang and a former subject of Cai Xingzong's commandery; trusted by Wang Xuanymou, he was sent on a visit, and Cai Xingzong thereupon said to him: "The Commandant must be deeply fearful and alarmed."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanymou's registrar Bao Farong was a native of Dongyang and a former subject of Xingzong's commandery; trusted by Xuanymou, he was sent on a visit, and Xingzong thereupon said to him: "The Commandant must be deeply fearful and alarmed."

sentences.zh: 」法榮曰：「領軍比日殆不復食，夜亦不眠，常言收已在門，不保俄頃。

translations.literal: Bao Farong said: "The Commandant of late can scarcely eat; he does not sleep at night and constantly says that arrest is already at the gate and he cannot be assured even for a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Farong said: "The Commandant of late can scarcely eat; he does not sleep at night and constantly says that arrest is already at the gate and he cannot be assured even for a moment."

sentences.zh: 」興宗曰：「領軍憂懼，當為方略，那得坐待禍至。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "If the Commandant is fearful and alarmed, he ought to devise a plan—how can he sit and wait for disaster to arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "If the Commandant is fearful and alarmed, he ought to devise a plan—how can he sit and wait for disaster to arrive?"

sentences.zh: 」初，玄謨舊部曲猶有三千人，廢帝頗疑之，徹配監者。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Xuanymou's old retainers still numbered three thousand; the Deposed Former Emperor was quite suspicious of them and reassigned them under overseers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuanymou's old retainers still numbered three thousand; the Deposed Former Emperor was quite suspicious of them and reassigned them under overseers.

sentences.zh: 玄謨太息深怨，啟留五百人巖山營墓，事猶未畢，少帝欲獵，又悉喚還城。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanymou sighed deeply and harbored deep resentment; he requested that five hundred men remain at Yanshan to build his tomb—the work was not yet finished when the Deposed Former Emperor wished to hunt and summoned them all back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanymou sighed deeply and harbored deep resentment; he requested that five hundred men remain at Yanshan to build his tomb—the work was not yet finished when the Deposed Former Emperor wished to hunt and summoned them all back to the city.

sentences.zh: 巖兵在中堂，興宗勸以此眾舉事，曰：「當今以領軍威名，率此為朝廷唱始，事便立克。

translations.literal: The Yanshan troops were in the central hall; Cai Xingzong urged that with this force they rise up, saying: "At present, with the Commandant's formidable reputation, leading these men to initiate action for the court, the matter would be settled at once."
translations.idiomatic: The Yanshan troops were in the central hall; Xingzong urged that with this force they rise up, saying: "At present, with the Commandant's formidable reputation, leading these men to initiate action for the court, the matter would be settled at once."

sentences.zh: 領軍雖復失腳，自可乘輿處分。

translations.literal: Even if the Commandant should again lose his footing, he could himself take the imperial carriage and dispose affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Commandant should again stumble, he could himself mount the imperial carriage and dispose affairs.

sentences.zh: 禍殆不測，勿失事機。

translations.literal: Disaster is hard to foretell—do not lose the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is hard to foresee—do not let the opportunity slip.

sentences.zh: 君還，可白領軍如此。

translations.literal: When you return, you may report this to the Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When you return, tell the Commandant as much.

sentences.zh: 」玄謨遣法榮報曰：「此亦未易可行，期當不泄君言。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanymou sent Bao Farong back with a reply: "This too is not easily feasible; I expect I shall not reveal your words."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanymou sent Farong back with a reply: "This too is not easily feasible; I expect I shall not reveal your words."

sentences.zh: 」太宗踐祚，玄謨責所親故吏郭季產、女婿韋希真等曰：「當艱難時，周旋輩無一言相扣發者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Wang Xuanymou reproached his close associates and former clerks Guo Jichan, his son-in-law Wei Xizhen, and others, saying: "In those difficult times, none of my companions said a single word to urge me to act."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Xuanymou reproached his close associates and former clerks Guo Jichan, his son-in-law Wei Xizhen, and others, saying: "In those difficult times, none of my companions said a single word to urge me to act."

sentences.zh: 」季產曰：「蔡尚書令包法榮所道，非不會機，但大事難行爾，季產言亦何益。

translations.literal: Guo Jichan said: "What Minister Cai told Bao Farong was not without understanding of the moment, but great affairs are hard to carry out; what use would Jichan's words have been?"
translations.idiomatic: Jichan said: "What Minister Cai told Bao Farong was not without understanding of the moment, but great affairs are hard to carry out; what use would Jichan's words have been?"

sentences.zh: 」玄謨有慚色。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanymou looked ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanymou looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍劉道隆為帝所寵信，專統禁兵，乘輿嘗夜幸著作佐郎江斅宅，興宗馬車從道隆從車後過，興宗謂曰：「劉公！

translations.literal: General of the Right Guards Liu Daolong was favored and trusted by the emperor and exclusively commanded the palace guard; the imperial carriage once visited at night the residence of Jiang Xiao, aide in the Secretariat for Compilation; Cai Xingzong's carriage passed behind Liu Daolong's escort carriage, and Cai Xingzong said: "Master Liu!"
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Guards Liu Daolong was favored and trusted by the emperor and exclusively commanded the palace guard; the imperial carriage once visited at night the residence of Jiang Xiao, aide in the Secretariat for Compilation; Xingzong's carriage passed behind Daolong's escort carriage, and Xingzong said: "Master Liu!"

sentences.zh: 比日思一閑寫。

translations.literal: Of late I have wished for a quiet talk.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have wished for a quiet word together.

sentences.zh: 」道隆深達此旨，掐興宗手曰：「蔡公！

translations.literal: Liu Daolong deeply grasped this intent, squeezed Cai Xingzong's hand, and said: "Master Cai!"
translations.idiomatic: Daolong deeply grasped this intent, squeezed Xingzong's hand, and said: "Master Cai!"

sentences.zh: 勿多言。

translations.literal: Do not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Say no more.

sentences.zh: 」帝每因朝宴，捶毆群臣，自驃騎大將軍建安王休仁以下，侍中袁愍孫等，咸見陵曳，唯興宗得免。

translations.literal: At every court banquet the emperor would beat and assault the ministers; from General of Agile Cavalry Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, down to Palace Attendant Yuan Minsun and others, all were humiliated and dragged about—only Cai Xingzong was spared.
translations.idiomatic: At every court banquet the emperor would beat and assault the ministers; from General of Agile Cavalry Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, down to Palace Attendant Yuan Minsun and others, all were humiliated and dragged about—only Xingzong was spared.

sentences.zh: 頃之，太宗定大事。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Taizong settled the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Taizong brought the great affair to its conclusion.

sentences.zh: 是夜，廢帝橫屍在大醫閣口，興宗謂尚書右僕射王景文曰：「此雖凶悖，要是天下之主，宜使喪禮粗足。

translations.literal: That night the Deposed Former Emperor lay dead across the entrance to the Grand Physician's Office; Cai Xingzong said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jingwen: "Though he was violent and perverse, he was after all sovereign of the realm; the funeral rites ought at least to be roughly adequate."
translations.idiomatic: That night the Deposed Former Emperor lay dead across the entrance to the Grand Physician's Office; Xingzong said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jingwen: "Though he was violent and perverse, he was after all sovereign of the realm; the funeral rites ought at least to be roughly adequate."

sentences.zh: 若直如此，四海必將乘人。」

translations.literal: If it is simply left like this, the four seas will surely take advantage of our disorder."
translations.idiomatic: If matters are simply left as they are, all under heaven will surely exploit our disorder."

sentences.zh: 時諸方並舉兵反，國家所保，唯丹陽、淮南數郡，其間諸縣，或已應賊。

translations.literal: At that time all regions were raising troops in rebellion; what the state could still hold was only several commanderies of Danyang and Huainan, and among their counties some had already joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every region was raising troops in rebellion; the state could still hold only a few commanderies of Danyang and Huainan, and among their counties some had already gone over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 東兵已至永世，宮省危懼，上集群臣以謀成敗。

translations.literal: Eastern troops had already reached Yongshi; the palace offices were fearful and alarmed; the emperor assembled the ministers to deliberate success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern troops had already reached Yongshi; the palace offices were stricken with fear; the emperor assembled his ministers to weigh success or failure.

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「今普天圖逆，人有異志，宜鎮之以靜，以至信侍人。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said: "Now under heaven all plot rebellion and men harbor divergent intent; you should calm them with stillness and treat people with utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "Now under heaven all plot rebellion and men harbor divergent intent; you should calm them with stillness and treat people with utmost sincerity."

sentences.zh: 比者逆徒親戚，布在宮省，若繩之以法，則土崩立至，宜明罪不相及之義。

translations.literal: Recently the kinsmen of rebels are spread through the palace offices; if you bind them with the law, collapse will come at once—you should make clear the principle that guilt does not extend to relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the kinsmen of rebels are spread through the palace offices; if you bind them with the law, collapse will come at once—you should declare clearly that guilt does not extend to relatives.

sentences.zh: 物情既定，人有戰心，六軍精勇，器甲犀利，以待不習之兵，其勢相萬耳。

translations.literal: Once popular sentiment is settled, men will have the will to fight; the Six Armies are elite and brave, their weapons and armor sharp, to await troops unaccustomed to war—the odds are ten thousand to one.
translations.idiomatic: Once popular sentiment is settled, men will take heart for battle; the Six Armies are elite and brave, armed with sharp weapons and armor, against troops unaccustomed to war—the odds are ten thousand to one.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿憂。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to worry.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to set your mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 加游擊將軍，未拜，遷尚書右僕射，尋領衛尉，又領兗州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Attacks at Large; before he received the appointment he was transferred to Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat; soon after he also held the office of Commandant of the Guard, and additionally served as Grand Rectifier for Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Attacks at Large, but before he could formally assume the title he was made Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat; he soon added the post of Commandant of the Guard and also served as Grand Rectifier for Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂興宗曰：「諸處未定，殷琰已復同逆。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Xingzong: "Various places are not yet settled, and Yin Yan has again joined the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong (Liu Yu) said to Cai Xingzong: "The various regions are still unsettled, and Yin Yan has once more thrown in with the rebels."

sentences.zh: 頃日人情云何？

translations.literal: How has popular sentiment been in recent days?
translations.idiomatic: What is the mood of the people these days?

sentences.zh: 事當濟不？

translations.literal: Will the affair succeed or not?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think we shall prevail?

sentences.zh: 」興宗曰：「逆之與順，臣無以辨。

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "As to rebel and loyal, your servant has no way to distinguish."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong replied: "Between rebellion and loyalty, I cannot clearly tell which side holds sway."

sentences.zh: 今商旅斷絕，而米甚豐賤，四方雲合，而人情更安，以此卜之，清蕩可必。

translations.literal: Now merchants and travelers are cut off, yet rice is very abundant and cheap; from the four directions men gather like clouds, yet popular sentiment is more at ease—by this one may divinate: pacification is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Trade has all but stopped, yet grain is plentiful and cheap; rebels converge from every quarter, yet the people remain remarkably calm. By these signs, I am certain the realm will be pacified.

sentences.zh: 但臣之所憂，更在事後，猶羊公言既平之後，方當勞聖慮耳。

translations.literal: But what your servant worries about lies rather in what comes after, just as Duke Yang said: only after pacification will it truly tax the sage's concern.
translations.idiomatic: My concern, however, lies after victory—as Yang Hu once observed, it is only once order is restored that Your Majesty's mind will truly be burdened.

sentences.zh: 」尚書褚淵以手板築興宗，興宗言之不已，上曰：「如卿言。

translations.literal: Minister Chu Yuan tapped Xingzong with his name tablet; Xingzong kept speaking without stopping; the emperor said: "As you say."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chu Yuan rapped Xingzong with his tablet to silence him, but Xingzong would not stop; the emperor said: "You speak truly."

sentences.zh: 」赭圻平，函送袁顗首，敕從登南掖門樓觀之，興宗漼然流涕，上不悅。

translations.literal: When Zheqi was pacified, Yuan Yan's head was sent in a casket; the emperor ordered his followers to ascend the tower of the Southern Side Gate to view it; Xingzong wept profusely; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheqi fell, Yuan Yan's head arrived in a box; the emperor commanded his attendants to climb the tower of the Southern Side Gate to view it. Xingzong burst into tears, and the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 事平，封興宗始昌縣伯，食邑五百戶；

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Xingzong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shichang County with a fief of five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Cai Xingzong was created Marquis of Shichang with a fief of five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 固讓不許，封樂安縣伯，邑三百戶，國秩吏力，終以不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was not permitted; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Le'an County with a fief of three hundred households, with stipend and clerical support for the fief, but in the end he accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly refused until the court relented and offered Le'an instead, with three hundred households plus stipend and clerical staff—but he declined even that.

sentences.zh: 時殷琰據壽陽為逆，遣輔國將軍劉勔攻圍。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Yan held Shouyang in rebellion; the court dispatched General Who Supports the State Liu Mian to attack and besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan was then holding Shouyang in rebellion, and the court sent General Liu Mian to invest the city.

sentences.zh: 四方既平，琰嬰城固守，上使中書為詔譬琰，興宗曰：「天下既定，是琰思過之日，陛下宜賜手詔數行以相私慰。

translations.literal: Once the four quarters were settled, Yan barricaded the city and held firm; the emperor had the Secretariat draft an edict to persuade Yan; Xingzong said: "The realm is already settled—this is the day for Yan to reflect on his faults; Your Majesty should bestow a personal edict of several lines to comfort him privately."
translations.idiomatic: With the realm largely pacified, Yan still held the walled city; the emperor had the Secretariat draft an edict to win him over. Xingzong urged: "The empire is settled—it is time for Yan to repent. Your Majesty should send him a personal note of a few lines as a private reassurance."

sentences.zh: 今直中書為詔，彼必疑謂非真，未是所以速清方難也。

translations.literal: If now the Secretariat alone drafts the edict, he will surely suspect it is not genuine—this is not the way to speedily clear regional troubles.
translations.idiomatic: A routine Secretariat edict will only make him suspect it is a ruse—that is no way to resolve this lingering crisis quickly.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: The advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 琰得詔，謂劉勔詐造，果不敢降。

translations.literal: When Yan received the edict, he judged that Liu Mian had forged it, and indeed did not dare to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan received the edict and assumed Liu Mian had fabricated it; as expected, he refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 攻戰經時，久乃歸順。

translations.literal: Attack and battle continued for a long time; only after a long while did he submit.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting dragged on for months before he finally capitulated.

sentences.zh: 先徐州刺史薛安都據彭城反，後遣使歸順。

translations.literal: First the Governor of Xu Province Xue Andu held Pengcheng in rebellion; afterward he sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Province governor Xue Andu had seized Pengcheng and rebelled; he later sent envoys offering submission.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年冬，遣張永率軍迎之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Taishi, Zhang Yong was dispatched leading an army to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Taishi 2, the court dispatched Zhang Yong at the head of an army to receive him.

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「安都遣使歸順，此誠不虛。

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "Andu's dispatch of envoys to submit—this is truly not false."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said: "Andu's offer of submission through envoys is surely sincere."

sentences.zh: 今宜撫之以和，即安所蒞，不過須單使及咫尺書耳。

translations.literal: Now one ought to reassure him with peace; as for what brings peace, nothing more is needed than a lone envoy and a letter of a few inches.
translations.idiomatic: He should be won over with conciliation—a single envoy and a brief letter would suffice.

sentences.zh: 若以重兵迎之，勢必疑懼，或能招引北虜，為患不測。

translations.literal: If one greets him with a heavy army, he will surely become suspicious and fearful, and may be able to summon the northern barbarians—calamity beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Sending a large force will only frighten him into suspicion and may provoke the Northern Wei—a disaster whose scale cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 叛臣釁重，必宜翦戮，則比者所宥，亦已弘矣。

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers whose offense is grave ought surely to be cut down; yet the mercy recently extended has already been ample.
translations.idiomatic: Treasonous ministers deserve execution, yet the amnesty already granted has been generous enough.

sentences.zh: 況安都外據強地，密邇邊關，考之國計，尤宜馴養。

translations.literal: Moreover Andu holds strong territory abroad, close to the border passes—in reckoning the state's interest, he especially ought to be tamed and nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Andu moreover holds strategic territory on the frontier; from the standpoint of statecraft, he is best handled with restraint and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 如其遂叛，將生旰食之憂。

translations.literal: If he then rebels, there will arise the worry of eating until sunrise.
translations.idiomatic: Should he turn traitor after all, the court will face sleepless nights of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 彭城險固，兵強將勇，圍之既難，攻不可拔，疆塞之虞，二三宜慮，臣為朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: Pengcheng is perilous and firm, its troops strong and its generals brave—besieging it is already hard, assaulting it cannot be taken; anxieties over the frontier passes—two or three ought to be considered—I worry on the court's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng is strongly fortified with brave troops and capable generals—difficult to besiege, impossible to storm. The risk to our border defenses is grave on several counts. I fear for the court's sake.

sentences.zh: 」時張永已行，不見從。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yong had already set out; the advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Yong was already marching; his counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 安都聞大軍過淮，嬰城自守，要取索虜。

translations.literal: Andu heard the great army cross the Huai; he barricaded the city and held himself, summoning the Xianbei barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that a large army was crossing the Huai, Andu shut himself in Pengcheng and sought aid from the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 永戰大敗，又值寒雪，死者十八九，遂失淮北四州。

translations.literal: Yong was utterly defeated in battle; moreover he encountered cold snow; eight or nine of ten died; thus the four northern Huai provinces were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong suffered a crushing defeat in bitter snow; eight or nine men in ten perished, and the four provinces north of the Huai were lost.

sentences.zh: 其先見如此。

translations.literal: His prior foresight was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such had been his foresight.

sentences.zh: 初，永敗問至，上在乾明殿，先召司徒建安王休仁，又召興宗，謂休仁曰：「吾慚蔡僕射。

translations.literal: At first, when news of Yong's defeat arrived, the emperor was in the Qianming Hall; he first summoned the Minister of Works, Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, then summoned Xingzong, and said to Xiuren: "I am ashamed before Vice Director Cai."
translations.idiomatic: When word of Zhang Yong's defeat first arrived, the emperor was in the Qianming Hall. He summoned Minister Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, then called in Xingzong and told Xiuren: "I owe Vice Director Cai an apology."

sentences.zh: 」以敗書示興宗，曰：「我愧卿。」

translations.literal: He showed Xingzong the dispatch of defeat and said: "I am ashamed before you."
translations.idiomatic: He showed Xingzong the defeat report and said: "I was wrong to ignore you."

sentences.zh: 三年春，出為使持節、都督郢州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he went out as Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Area Commander for all military affairs of Ying Province, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year he was posted out as military governor and Governor of Ying Province, with the title General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 坐詣尚書切論以何始真為諮議參軍，初不被許，後又重陳，上怒，貶號平西將軍，尋又復號。

translations.literal: For going to the Secretariat and arguing forcefully to have He Shizhen made Advising Commander, at first not permitted, then arguing again, the emperor was angered; his title was demoted to General Who Pacifies the West; soon his former title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for pressing the Secretariat to appoint He Shizhen as Advising Commander—first overruled, then insisting again until the emperor grew angry and reduced his title to General Who Pacifies the West, though it was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 初，吳興丘珍孫言論常侵興宗。

translations.literal: At first Qiu Zhensun of Wuxing in speech and argument often encroached on Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhensun of Wuxing had long been verbally aggressive toward Cai Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 珍孫子景先，人才甚美，興宗與之周旋。

translations.literal: Zhensun's son Jingxian was a man of great talent and beauty; Xingzong associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhensun's son Jingxian was an exceptionally talented young man, and Xingzong cultivated his friendship.

sentences.zh: 及景先為鄱陽郡，值晉安王子勛為逆，轉在竟陵，為吳喜所殺。

translations.literal: When Jingxian was in Poyang commandery, it happened that Liu Zilun, Prince of Jin'an, rebelled; he was transferred to Jingling and was killed by Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxian was serving in Poyang, Liu Zilun, Prince of Jin'an, rose in rebellion; Jingxian was transferred to Jingling, where Wu Xi killed him.

sentences.zh: 母老女稚，流離夏口。

translations.literal: His mother was old and his daughter young; they wandered destitute at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: His aged mother and young daughter were left stranded and destitute at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 興宗至郢州，親自臨哭，致其喪柩家累，令得東還。

translations.literal: When Xingzong reached Ying Province, he personally went to mourn; he sent back the coffin and the household dependents, enabling them to return east.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post at Ying Province, Xingzong went in person to mourn, arranged the return of the coffin and the bereaved family, and saw them safely back east.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，遷鎮東將軍、會稽太守，加散騎常侍，尋領兵置佐，加都督會稽、東陽、新安、永嘉、臨海五郡諸軍事，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was transferred to General Who Guards the East and Governor of Kuaiji, added as Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse; soon he also received military aides; added as Area Commander for military affairs of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai; granted one set of horns and drums.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was promoted to General Who Guards the East and Governor of Kuaiji, with the added title Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse; he soon received military staff and authority over five commanderies—Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai—and was granted an honorary guard of horns and drums.

sentences.zh: 會稽多諸豪右，不遵王憲。

translations.literal: Kuaiji had many powerful gentry who did not observe the royal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was home to many powerful clans who flouted imperial law.

sentences.zh: 又幸臣近習，參半宮省，封略山湖，妨民害治。

translations.literal: Moreover favored ministers and close attendants, half filling the palace offices, enclosed and surveyed mountains and lakes, obstructing the people and harming governance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favorites and court intimates, who thronged the palace bureaucracy, had seized mountains and lakes to the people's detriment.

sentences.zh: 興宗皆以法繩之。

translations.literal: Xingzong bound them all by law.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong held them all accountable under the law.

sentences.zh: 會土全實，民物殷阜，王公妃主，邸舍相望，橈亂在所，大為民患，子息滋長，督責無窮。

translations.literal: The land of Kuaiji was whole and rich, its people and goods abundant; princes, nobles, imperial consorts, and princesses—their mansions looked out on one another; interference was everywhere, greatly harming the people; their sons and descendants multiplied, and exactions and demands were endless.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was fertile and prosperous, and princes, nobles, and imperial in-laws built mansion upon mansion. Their ceaseless encroachments and ever-multiplying demands tormented the common people.

sentences.zh: 興宗悉啟罷省。

translations.literal: Xingzong memorialized to abolish and eliminate them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong petitioned to have them all abolished.

sentences.zh: 又陳原諸逋負，解遣雜役，並見從。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to remit all overdue obligations and to release miscellaneous corvée laborers; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also secured remission of unpaid levies and the release of miscellaneous conscript labor—all of which the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三吳舊有鄉射禮，久不復修，興宗行之，禮儀甚整。

translations.literal: The Three Wu region formerly had the village archery rite; for a long time it was not restored; Xingzong performed it—the ritual was very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu had once maintained the village archery ceremony, long neglected; Xingzong revived it with exemplary propriety.

sentences.zh: 先是元嘉中，羊玄保為郡，亦行鄉射。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Yuanjia era, Yang Xuanbao as governor also performed the village archery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era, Yang Xuanbao as governor had likewise held the village archery rite.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，興宗與尚書令袁粲、右僕射褚淵、中領軍劉勔、鎮軍將軍沈攸之同被顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong died, Xingzong together with Director Yuan Can, Vice Director Chu Yuan, Commandant of the Center Liu Mian, and General Who Guards the Army Shen Youzhi were jointly entrusted with the dying command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong died, Xingzong was named to the regency council alongside Director Yuan Can, Vice Director Chu Yuan, Commandant Liu Mian, and General Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 以興宗為使持節、都督荊、湘、雍、益、梁、寧、南、北秦八州諸軍事、征西將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史，加班劍二十人，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Xingzong was appointed Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Area Commander for military affairs of the eight provinces Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Conquers the West, Grand Master with Emoluments Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jing Province; twenty guards with half-drawn swords were added; Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong was made military governor of eight western provinces with the title General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of the First Order, Governor of Jing Province, attended by twenty sword-bearing guards, retaining his post as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 被徵還都。

translations.literal: He was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時右軍將軍王道隆任參內政，權重一時，躡履到前，不敢就席，良久方去，竟不呼坐。

translations.literal: At that time General of the Right Guards Wang Daolong held a share in internal governance, his authority weighty for a time; he walked softly on tiptoe to the fore; he did not dare to take a seat; only after a long while did he depart—and in the end was never invited to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong, General of the Right Guards, then wielded enormous power in court affairs. He crept forward on tiptoe, dared not sit down, lingered awkwardly, and finally left—never once invited to take a seat.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，中書舍人秋當詣太子詹事王曇首，不敢坐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Palace Secretary Qiu Dang visited the Grand Tutor of the Heir Wang Tanshou and did not dare to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanjia era, Palace Secretary Qiu Dang called on Grand Tutor Wang Tanshou and did not dare to sit.

sentences.zh: 其後中書舍人王弘為太祖所愛遇，上謂曰：「卿欲作士人，得就王球坐，乃當判耳。

translations.literal: Thereafter Palace Secretary Wang Hong was favored by Emperor Taizu; the emperor said to him: "If you wish to become a gentleman of standing, you may go sit with Wang Qiu—that would truly be a distinction."
translations.idiomatic: Later, Palace Secretary Wang Hong won Emperor Taizu's favor. The emperor told him: "If you wish to be accepted as a gentleman, try sitting with Wang Qiu—that would mark a genuine rise in standing."

sentences.zh: 殷、劉並雜，無所知也。

translations.literal: Yin and Liu are both mixed company—they understand nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin and Liu clans are vulgar company—they would not understand such things.

sentences.zh: 若往詣球，可稱旨就席。

translations.literal: If you go visit Qiu, you may cite the imperial intent and take a seat.
translations.idiomatic: If you visit Qiu, cite my words as authorization and take a seat.

sentences.zh: 」球舉扇曰：「若不得爾。

translations.literal: Qiu raised his fan and said: "If it cannot be so."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu lifted his fan and said: "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 」弘還，依事啟聞，帝曰：「我便無如此何。

translations.literal: Hong returned and reported the matter as it stood; the emperor said: "Then there is nothing I can do about it."
translations.idiomatic: Hong returned and reported what had happened; the emperor said: "Well, then I cannot force the matter."

sentences.zh: 」五十年中，有此三事。

translations.literal: Within fifty years, there were these three incidents.
translations.idiomatic: In the span of fifty years, only these three such incidents occurred.

sentences.zh: 道隆等以興宗強正，不欲使擁兵上流，改為中書監、左光祿大夫，開府儀同三司、常侍如故，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Daolong and the others, because Xingzong was forceful and upright, did not wish him to hold troops on the upper reaches; he was changed to Director of the Secretariat, Grand Master of Splendor on the Left, Grand Master with Emoluments Equal to the Three Excellencies, Regular Attendant as before; he firmly declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong and his faction, wary of the upright and unyielding Xingzong commanding troops upriver, reassigned him to Director of the Secretariat and Grand Master of Splendor on the Left with the honors of the Three Excellencies—but Xingzong firmly refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 興宗幼立風概，家行尤謹，奉宗姑，事寡嫂，養孤兄子，有聞於世。

translations.literal: Xingzong in youth established moral bearing; his family conduct was especially careful—he served his husband's aunt, attended to his widowed sister-in-law, and reared his orphaned brother's son; he was renowned in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong displayed moral resolve from youth. His household conduct was exemplary: he cared for his paternal aunt, tended his widowed sister-in-law, and raised his orphaned nephew—winning widespread renown.

sentences.zh: 太子左率王錫妻范，聰明婦人也，有才藻學見，與錫弟僧達書，詰讓之曰：「昔謝太傅奉嫂王夫人如慈母，今蔡興宗亦有恭和之稱。

translations.literal: Fan, wife of Commander of the Left for the Heir Wang Xi, was an intelligent woman, possessed of literary talent and learning; she wrote to Xi's brother Sengda, reproaching him: "Formerly Grand Tutor Xie served his sister-in-law Lady Wang as a loving mother; now Cai Xingzong also bears the reputation of reverent harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Fan, wife of the Heir's Left Commander Wang Xi, was a brilliant woman of learning. In a letter reproaching Wang Xi's brother Sengda, she wrote: "Grand Tutor Xie once treated his sister-in-law Lady Wang as a mother would; today Cai Xingzong is likewise praised for his respectful tenderness toward kin."

sentences.zh: 」其為世所重如此。

translations.literal: He was thus esteemed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏早卒，一女甚幼，外甥袁顗始生彖而妻劉氏亦亡。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Liu died early; one daughter was very young; his sister's son Yuan Yan had just born Tan when Lady Liu also died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu died young, leaving a small daughter; his nephew Yuan Yan's son Tan was newborn when Lady Liu passed as well.

sentences.zh: 興宗姊，即顗母也，一孫一姪，躬自撫養，年齒相比，欲為婚姻，每見興宗，輒言此意。

translations.literal: Xingzong's elder sister was Yan's mother; one grandson and one nephew—she personally reared them; their ages were comparable; she wished to arrange a marriage; whenever she saw Xingzong, she would speak this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's elder sister—Yuan Yan's mother—raised grandson and nephew side by side, nearly of an age, and whenever she saw Xingzong she pressed her wish to unite them in marriage.

sentences.zh: 大明初，詔興宗女與南平王敬猷婚，興宗以姊生平之懷，屢經陳啟，答曰：「卿諸人欲各行己意，則國家何由得婚？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming, an edict ordered Xingzong's daughter to marry Prince Jingyou of Nanping; Xingzong, out of his sister's lifelong wish, repeatedly memorialized; the reply came: "If you all wish each to follow your own intent, how can the state arrange marriages?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming reign, an edict betrothed Xingzong's daughter to Prince Jingyou of Nanping. Citing his sister's lifelong wish, Xingzong memorialized repeatedly—but Emperor Xiaowu replied: "If everyone insists on their private wishes, how is the throne to arrange marriages at all?"

sentences.zh: 且姊言豈是不可違之處邪？

translations.literal: Moreover is your sister's word not a place where one cannot disobey?
translations.idiomatic: And is a sister's dying wish not something that ought to be honored?

sentences.zh: 」舊意既乖，彖亦他娶。

translations.literal: The original intent having gone astray, Tan also married elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: With that original plan undone, Tan married someone else.

sentences.zh: 其後彖家好不終，顗又禍敗，彖等淪廢當時，孤微理盡。

translations.literal: Thereafter Tan's household alliance did not reach its end; Yan again met calamity and ruin; Tan and the others were cast down and ruined in their time—orphaned, insignificant, reason exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's marriage ended unhappily; Yuan Yan met disaster and ruin; Tan and his kin fell into utter destitution—as though fate had exhausted every allowance for their line.

sentences.zh: 敬猷遇害，興宗女無子嫠居，名門高胄，多欲結姻，明帝亦敕適謝氏，興宗並不許，以女適彖。

translations.literal: Jingyou met with harm and was killed; Xingzong's daughter, childless, lived as a widow; noble gates and high pedigrees—many wished to forge marriage ties; Emperor Ming also ordered her to marry the Xie clan; Xingzong refused them all and gave his daughter to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingyou was killed, Xingzong's widowed and childless daughter drew offers from many eminent families; Emperor Ming himself ordered a match with the Xie clan—but Xingzong refused them all and gave her to Tan.

sentences.zh: 北地傅隆與廓相善，興宗脩父友敬。

translations.literal: Fu Long of Beidi was on good terms with Kuo; Xingzong maintained the courtesy due a father's friend.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long of Beidi had been close to Cai Kuo; Xingzong honored him as his father's friend.

sentences.zh: 景玄雅有父風，為中書郎，晉陵太守，太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Jingxuan elegantly possessed his father's style; he served as Secretariat Gentleman, Governor of Jinling, and Aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan inherited his father's distinguished bearing and held the posts of Secretariat Gentleman, Governor of Jinling, and Aide to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 昇明末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of the Shengming era.
translations.idiomatic: He died late in the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世重清談，士推素論，蔡廓雖業力弘正，而年位未高，一世名臣，風格皆出其下。

translations.literal: The Historian comments: The age prized pure talk; scholars promoted plain discourse; although Cai Kuo's accomplishment and virtue were grand and upright, his years and rank were not high—eminent ministers of a generation, their style all fell below his.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian writes: In an age that prized refined discourse and plain principle, Cai Kuo's conduct and integrity were surpassing—yet because his years and rank had not risen high, the era's celebrated ministers all fell short of his stature.

sentences.zh: 及其固辭銓衡，恥為志屈，豈不知選錄同體，義無偏斷乎！

translations.literal: When he firmly declined the balances of selection, ashamed that his will was bent—did he not know that selection and appointment form one body, and in principle there can be no partial judgment!
translations.idiomatic: When he steadfastly refused the post of personnel selection, refusing to bend his principles—did he not know that the selector and the selected are one enterprise, and impartiality is the very duty of the office?

sentences.zh: 良以主闇時難，不欲居通塞之任也。

translations.literal: Truly it was because the ruler was dim and the times difficult—he did not wish to hold an office of clear passage and blockage.
translations.idiomatic: In truth, the sovereign was obscured and the times perilous—he would not accept an office where one must decide who passes and who is blocked.

sentences.zh: 遠矣哉！

translations.literal: How distant!
translations.idiomatic: How remote such integrity now seems!
